INTRODUCTION

Hello! We are excited to welcome you to Friendly Fence & Roofing.

Here at Friendly Fence & Roofing, we pride ourselves on creating a warm, team-focused atmosphere where cooperation and support are central to our operations. We hope that you will find our company to be a welcoming, engaging, and fair place to work!

This handbook presents a number of key concepts for our company. Some of these represent legal standards that we adhere to. Other aspects outline our expectations for employees and what employees can expect from us. We strongly encourage you to read this handbook in its entirety and keep it in a location where you can easily access it as a valuable resource and reference.

SECTION 1: ADMINISTRATIVE POLICIES AND PROCEDURES

Employment At-Will

Employment with Friendly Fence & Roofing is on an at-will basis. Because of this, employment may be terminated by either Friendly Fence & Roofing or the employee with or without cause, and with or without notice, at any time.

No one other than the Friendly Fence & Roofing owner/president has the authority to create an employment relationship other than on an at will basis, and he/she may only do so based upon a signed written agreement between the owner/president and the employee. Nothing contained in this or any other document provided to the employee is intended to be, nor should it be, construed as a contract that employment or any benefit will be continued for any period of time.

Furthermore, the terms and conditions of employment with Friendly Fence & Roofing may be modified at the sole discretion of Friendly Fence & Roofing with or without cause and with or without notice. Examples of the types of terms and conditions of employment that are within the sole discretion of Friendly Fence & Roofing include, but are not limited to,: promotion; demotion; transfers; hiring and discharge decisions; compensation; benefits; qualifications; discipline; layoff or recall; rules; hours and schedules; work assignments; job duties and responsibilities; reduction, cessation, or expansion of operations; sale, relocation, merger, or consolidation of operations; determinations concerning the use of equipment, methods, or facilities; or any other terms and conditions that Friendly Fence & Roofing may determine to be necessary for the safe, efficient, and economic operation of its business.

Protected Classes

Multiple policies within this handbook refer to “protected classes.” Protected classes include, but are not limited to, the following:

race,

color,

sex (including pregnancy),

religion,

age,

national origin or ancestry,

physical or mental disability,

genetic information,

veteran status, and

any other considerations made unlawful by federal, state, or local laws.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Friendly Fence & Roofing provides equal opportunities to all employees regardless of membership or perceived membership in a protected class. All such discrimination is unlawful and prohibited by Friendly Fence & Roofing. Equal employment opportunity applies to all personnel decisions and actions, including but not limited to: hiring, promotion, termination, compensation, leave of absence, and training.

Immigration Laws

Although Friendly Fence & Roofing does not unlawfully discriminate based upon citizenship status or national origin, Friendly Fence & Roofing requires that all employees be eligible to work within the United States. In compliance with the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986, Friendly Fence & Roofing requires that all employees have a completed Employment Eligibility Verification Form I-9, including providing necessary documentation establishing identity and employment eligibility.

If you have any questions regarding employment eligibility verification, please speak with management.

Reasonable Accommodation for Pregnancy and Disability

Friendly Fence & Roofing will make a reasonable accommodation for the known disability of any qualified individual who is otherwise able to perform the essential functions of his/her position. Reasonable accommodations include those that do not cause an undue hardship on the company or its employees. Any accommodation that creates an unsafe working environment for either the employee, other employees, or customers will be deemed to be unreasonable for the purposes of this policy.

Reasonable accommodations may be available to individuals with both permanent and temporary disabilities, and options may include transfers to positions with less strenuous or hazardous physical requirements.

Employees or applicants who have a disability, including pregnancy, should speak with management regarding any needed accommodations. Management will engage in an interactive process with the employee to determine whether a reasonable accommodation can be made. Management reserves the right to require medical certification of any accommodations required.

Please note: employees who are currently using illegal substances or improperly using restricted substances, such as prescription medication, are excluded from this policy.

Commitment to Diversity

At Friendly Fence & Roofing, we are committed to honoring the diverse backgrounds represented by our employees. This diversity is a source of strength, and, as such, we will strive to provide all employees the opportunity to participate and contribute to the success of Friendly Fence & Roofing. To that end, Friendly Fence & Roofing will accommodate special requests that do not constitute a threat to safety of the employee, other employees, or customers or present an undue hardship on the company or its other employees.

If an employee or applicant requires an accommodation based upon a religious belief or practice, he/she should speak with management immediately to determine whether an accommodation can be made. Similarly, if management becomes aware through other methods that a religious accommodation may be required, management may approach any impacted employee(s).

Similarly, Friendly Fence & Roofing strives to make its policies and practices fair to all employees and applicants. However, if any policy or practice of Friendly Fence & Roofing impacts an employee or applicant based upon his/her membership in a particular group or class (i.e., a “protected class”), the employee or applicant should speak with management regarding his/her concerns.

We encourage all employees and applicants to present his/her concerns in writing, as this method allows management the greatest opportunity to fully consider the area of concern. However, employees and applicants may also bring their concerns to management verbally. Management will engage in an interactive process with the impacted employee(s) to determine what, if any, reasonable accommodation may be made. If more than one reasonable accommodation exists, management reserves the right to make the final determination regarding the method or accommodation implemented.

Complaint Reporting Procedure

Although Friendly Fence & Roofing strives to make our company a professional and friendly place to work, there may be times when an employee feels that this has not occurred. In the event that an employee wishes to place a complaint, either about another employee or about a company practice, he/she is strongly encouraged to do so. Especially when that concern is regarding an incident of unlawful discrimination, sexual harassment, other harassment, retaliation, or denial of accommodation, Friendly Fence & Roofing recommends that an employee present a formal complaint to management so that the employee’s concern may be thoroughly investigated and, if found to be substantiated, addressed.

If you believe that you have been subject to or witnessed illegal discrimination, including sexual or other forms of unlawful harassment, you should complain directly to your immediate supervisor. If your immediate supervisor is directly involved, does not address your concerns, or you feel uncomfortable presenting your concerns to your immediate supervisor, you should report your concerns to any other member of management.

You are strongly encouraged to present your concerns in writing. A form for submission of a complaint can be obtained through asking your supervisor or any other member of management, and all employees are encouraged, but not required, to use this form if making a written complaint. However, if you are unable to do so, you may also lodge a complaint verbally.

If a supervisor receives a complaint from an employee, he/she is required to report the complaint to upper management for investigation. Furthermore, supervisors are required to report ALL suspected harassment, discrimination, or retaliation directly to management, even if no formal complaint has been placed by an employee. Management and supervisors will be held responsible for any discrimination, harassment, or retaliation that they commit or allow subordinates to commit. Failure to report discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or a complaint to upper management will be considered a violation of this policy.

All complaints will be thoroughly investigated by management in a manner ensuring, to the best of management’s ability, the confidentiality of all involved parties. Furthermore, all information concerning a complaint or occurrence will be kept on a “need to know” basis, and details will not be shared with uninvolved parties unless required by law.

If the investigation determines that conduct was performed against company policy or legal requirements, management will take immediate and appropriate corrective action, up to and including immediate termination of employment for any offending party.

Friendly Fence & Roofing will not tolerate or permit retaliation for filing a complaint by management, employees, or third parties.

Suggestions and Ideas

At Friendly Fence & Roofing, we encourage all employees to present any suggestions or ideas for improvement to their supervisors or management. We firmly believe that sometimes some of the best ideas come from those people who are in the field, day in and day out. As such, management will take any suggestions seriously and investigate which may be practical to implement on either an individual or company-wide basis. We encourage employees to provide a written suggestion; however, verbal discussions are also welcome at any time.

Employment Status

Employee benefits and overtime status are based upon a number of factors, including employment classifications. These classifications are presented below. A specific employee’s classification may be changed at any time with or without notice by management, so long as such change is compliant with federal and state legislation.

Exempt – employees whose job duties qualify for overtime and minimum wage regulation exemptions under federal and state law. These employees are normally expected to work full-time, and they are ineligible for overtime compensation.

Non-Exempt – employees who are compensated for any overtime worked. Please see the “Overtime” policy below for further details.

Part-Time Employees – employees who are not in a temporary status and who regularly are scheduled to work fewer than 40 hours each week. Part-time employees, may, on occasion, be required to work 40 or more hours per week; however, these requirements are considered temporary in nature. Part-time employees are generally ineligible for benefits. Any exceptions due to Federal or State law or individual agreement will be discussed related to the specific benefit.

Full-Time Employees – employees who are regularly scheduled at least 40 hours per week. Full-time employees are generally eligible for all benefits available for employees but are subject to the terms and conditions presented for each benefit.

Temporary Employees – employees who are hired to fulfill a temporary requirement for Friendly Fence & Roofing. These employees are hired for a specific duration or to fulfill a specific need. Temporary employees are not eligible for any benefits unless informed otherwise by management. Employment beyond the initially agreed upon period does not in any way imply a change in employment status without the express notification from management of a change in that status.

Company Waiting Period – the first 90 days after hire. During this period, employees are ineligible for employment benefits unless specific benefit details require an alternate waiting period duration.

Performance Evaluation and Merit-Based Pay Increases

We feel that you have the ability to be a strong asset to our company; however, even the best employees have room for improvement. Because of this, Friendly Fence & Roofing will create an ongoing dialogue with each employee regarding his/her performance. This dialogue will include both acknowledging the employee’s strengths and a frank and honest assessment of areas for improvement. Formal performance evaluations may also be provided; however, these may or may not occur on a set timetable, and they may or may not be associated with any changes in pay status. This system is designed to provide a basis for better understanding between you, your supervisor, and Friendly Fence & Roofing regarding your job performance, potential, and development within the company.

Friendly Fence & Roofing reserves the right to establish all pay system and pay rates. Pay increases occur more regularly in some job descriptions than others. Regardless, pay increases are based on several factors, including the overall success of Friendly Fence & Roofing. Other factors that may qualify employees for an increase in pay include: job performance, productivity, your current salary in your position's grade level, and your level of pay relative to what the industry is paying for similar qualities and talent. Please note: pay increases are not made based upon a set timetable.

Separation from Employment

As a reflection of Friendly Fence & Roofing status as an at-will employer, both Friendly Fence & Roofing and its employees may choose to end the employment relationship at any time, either with notice or without notice. However, Friendly Fence & Roofing requests that employees provide at least a 2-week notice of separation stating the employee’s final date of employment and the employee’s reason for separation. This notice may impact the employee’s eligibility for rehire, as well as any information provided to any future companies seeking employment verification. Similarly, when Friendly Fence & Roofing initiates a separation that is unrelated to an employee’s conduct, Friendly Fence & Roofing will attempt to provide notice to the employee.

Upon separation, employees will be paid for any pay outlined in the employee’s pay agreement. This will include all earned forms of non-discretionary pay. However, employees are ineligible for any fringe benefits, including discretionary pay (e.g., year-end bonuses, bonuses based upon overall company success), during the last month of his/her employment.

Employees will NOT be paid for any accrued but unused paid time off (PTO) upon separation of employment.Upon termination of employment, employees are required to return all issued Planet property. Examples of Friendly Fence & Roofing property include, but are not limited to, uniforms, credit cards, cellular telephones, and keys/access cards. Failure to do so may be considered theft, and Friendly Fence & Roofing reserves the right to take any and all legally available measures necessary to obtain stolen property.

An employee’s final paycheck may be issued Via Direct Deposit regardless of the employee’s participation in any direct deposit programs.

Work Week Logistics

The official work week for Friendly Fence & Roofing is from Friday at 12:00 am until Thursday at 11:59 pm. The Friendly Fence & Roofing office is generally open Monday through Friday from 7:00 am until 6:00 pm.

An employee’s work schedule is likely to vary either seasonally or each week based upon the anticipated and actual call volume. Although we attempt to schedule an 8-hour workday, employees are not guaranteed a full 8 hours of work, especially during our slower seasons. In addition, field employees are expected to remain working until their last call of the day has been completed safely and fully. Failure to do so will be considered a violation of this policy, and it may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment. Finally, employees may be required to work overtime when call volume demands. Please see the below “Overtime” policy for more information.

Breaks for Nursing Mothers

In accordance with federal legislation, Friendly Fence & Roofing will grant sufficient breaks to nursing mothers of infants under 12 months of age in order to express breast milk during the day. Nursing mothers should speak with management for additional information.

Overtime

There may be times when we cannot meet the needs of our customers during our standard business hours. When this occurs, employees may be required to work additional hours. Overtime hours may, at times, be assigned to individuals who volunteer; however, workload may demand that all employees work more than 40 hours in any one workweek. When overtime is mandatory, hours will be distributed as equitably as possible.

If an employee has not been assigned overtime hours, he/she MUST receive managerial approval prior to working overtime hours. Failure to do so will be considered a violation of this policy.

As required by law, all employees will be compensated for overtime based upon hours worked. Any benefit hours, such as paid time off (PTO), holiday, or other leave of absence time, will not be considered when determining and compensating for overtime.

Overtime is paid to all non-exempt employees according to state and federal regulations. All overtime compensation will be paid at an employee’s “regular rate of pay,” which includes all non-discretionary forms of compensation. Overtime premium pay will be provided for all hours worked in excess of forty (40) hours in any one workweek, and compensation will be equal to one and one-half times the employee’s regular rate of pay.

On-Call Status

As a residential service provider, Friendly Fence & Roofing responds to customers' emergencies 24 hours a day. To provide this service, employees who have specific job descriptions are expected to accept on-call status when requested by management. Employees will be informed if mandatory on-call status applies to them.

The following policies apply to on-call status:

Employees are expected to wear any assigned uniform when responding to all calls for service, even while on-call.

Employees on on-call status are expected to respond, via telephone, to a customer within 30 minutes of the customer’s original call.

It is the assigned employee’s responsibility to be on-call for the entire day, not just the night, if he/she is on-call on a holiday or weekend day.

The assigned employee is responsible for finding a replacement to cover his/her on-call time if he/she is on vacation when scheduled to be on-call. Management will assist employees who have a bona fide illness while on call.

Mandatory Company Meetings and On the Job Training

Friendly Fence & Roofing conducts meetings and company-wide training programs on a regular basis. When notified by management, employees are required to attend these meetings and programs as a mandatory requirement of their positions. Failure to do so will be considered an absence, and such absence will be evaluated in accordance with Friendly Fence & Roofing’s attendance policy.

In addition to company-wide training, supervisors are responsible for identifying and ensuring implementation of any needed on-the-job training for all employees who directly report to the supervisor. This type of training is generally based upon an employee’s specific need; however, it could also include additional training on new technologies, techniques, or growth opportunities. Examples may include one-on-one training with the supervisor or other employee, safety training in addition to standard safety meetings, participation in off-site training, and continuing education.

Training and meetings, when mandatory, will be conducted during regular working hours whenever possible.

Friendly Fence & Roofing will pay for any required training programs, including tuition costs and, unless specifically addressed as part of a disciplinary action, the employee’s time while attending mandatory training.

Employees may be tested from time to time to evaluate the effectiveness of any training program.

If you have any questions regarding mandatory meetings or training, please contact your supervisor.

State of Emergency/Inclement Weather

Management may, at times, choose to temporarily cease business operations due to extreme weather or other event. Examples include, but are not limited to, a blizzard, hurricane, forest fire, or earthquake. If management decides that Friendly Fence & Roofing will close, management will inform each employee by contacting the phone number he/she has on record and/or his/her assigned company-owned cell phone. A voicemail or text will be left if an employee cannot be directly reached.

Please note: although management will attempt to notify each employee, it is not management’s responsibility to ensure that each employee has actually received notification. Employees are responsible for ensuring that his/her phone number on file is up-to-date, and employees are also responsible for listening to any voicemails or reading any texts sent.

If an employee has NOT been notified that Friendly Fence & Roofing has ceased business operations, the employee should assume that Friendly Fence & Roofing will remain open for business. The employee should report to work as normal.

Especially if an employee lives in an area that is distant from Friendly Fence & Roofing main office, management encourages that employee to use his/her best discretion regarding the conditions in his/her area of residence, as well as the areas through which the employee would need to travel. Even when management chooses to still provide standard or reduced/emergency only business operations, employees may request leave if he/she feels that the conditions in his/her area of residence or logical path of travel present a significant safety hazard. However, management reserves the right to also evaluate safety conditions, and employees may be held liable for abuse of the emergency leave policy.

In the event that the mayor, governor, president, or other government official declares a state of emergency or a mandatory evacuation impacting either the employee’s home or Friendly Fence & Roofing office, Friendly Fence & Roofing will not retaliate in any way against an employee for not reporting for work as scheduled.

Any time taken off based upon inclement weather, states of emergency, or mandatory evacuations will be on an unpaid basis, regardless of whether management closes Friendly Fence & Roofing’ office. However, employees may choose to use any accrued but unused paid time off (PTO) during this unpaid leave.

Contagious Illnesses

Friendly Fence & Roofing shares concerns with many of its employees to reduce the chance of transmission of serious illnesses within our company. Because of this, we request that employees do not report to work if they are experiencing any extreme symptoms of illness. Although we request that employees “self-regulate” these symptoms, management may require employees stay home when experiencing symptoms.

Extreme symptoms include, but are not limited to:

Fever over 100°F

Vomiting or diarrhea

Severe sore throat

Severe headache or body aches not related to overexertion or injury

Excessive coughing or sneezing

Please note: if an employee is experiencing the above extreme symptoms and those extreme symptoms are the result of a medical condition that is not contagious (e.g., pregnancy or chronic condition), the employee is not required to stay home.

Management reserves the right to require employees to provide doctor’s certification for an employee’s fitness to resume full job duties after extended or regular absences. Furthermore, abuse of this policy will be considered a violation and may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment.

Paydays and Time Records

In accordance with all applicable state and federal laws, Friendly Fence & Roofing will compensate you for all of your time worked. To help ensure that employees are paid properly and no improper deductions are made, employees are responsible for:

accurately recording all time worked, including all travel and training time;

reviewing his/her time records for any unintentional errors prior to payroll submission;

ensuring all of the employee’s time records are submitted according to procedures established for his/her department;

submitting all vacation and/or leave hours based upon procedures established for his/her department, including all required signatures and/or approvals;

reviewing his/her paycheck promptly for any errors; and

immediately reporting any errors to management.

Please note: employees are strictly prohibited from engaging in “off-the-clock” work.

Time records not submitted on time and according to established procedures may result in errors in the employee’s pay, and correction of any errors may be delayed until subsequent pay periods.

Deductions from Pay

Friendly Fence & Roofing will automatically comply with all federal and state mandated deductions. Examples include federal, state, and/or local taxes and social security.

In addition to standard mandatory deductions made for all employees, Friendly Fence & Roofing will comply with all valid claims against the wages of employees, such as wage garnishments, child support orders, and other legally valid claims. An employee will be notified about the details of the garnishment or wage order. Please note: even if an employee is attempting to address financial difficulties with a creditor, Friendly Fence & Roofing is legally required to comply with all garnishment notices or orders as soon as they are received.

In addition to mandatory deductions, some employees may also elect to have specific voluntary deductions withheld for certain things, such as health insurance premiums or contributions to a retirement plan. All voluntary deductions will be presented to each employee for written approval prior to deductions being made.

Exempt Employee Deductions

The Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) limits the types of deductions that may be made from the pay of an exempt employee. In addition to those deductions outlined above, Friendly Fence & Roofing is permitted, by this statute, to make deductions for the following reasons:

Absence from work for one or more full days for personal reasons other than sickness or disability;

Absence from work for one or more full days due to sickness or disability of the employee;

Offset for amounts received as witness or jury fees, or for military pay;

Unpaid disciplinary suspensions of one or more full days for workplace misconduct; or

During the week an exempt employee begins work for the company or last week of employment, the employee will only be paid for actual hours worked.

Please note: Exempt employees will be required to use accrued paid time off (PTO) for full or partial day absences for personal reasons, sickness, or disability. However, an exempt employee’s pay will not be reduced for partial day absences if he/she has exhausted his/her PTO.

If an employee classified as exempt believes that an improper deduction has been taken from his/her pay, the employee should immediately report the error to management. The situation will be promptly investigated, and if it is found that an improper deduction has been made, Friendly Fence & Roofing will reimburse the employee for the improper deduction.

Time Records

Employees are responsible for ensuring that their time records are completed. It is considered a violation of this policy for an employee to:

Complete another employee’s time record;

Ask, allow, or require another employee to complete your time record;

Alter a time record with false information; or

Conceal or falsify a time record.

If any manager or employee asks you to violate any of the above policies or you become aware of another employee doing so, report the violation immediately to management.

Any violations of this policy may lead to disciplinary action, up to and including immediate termination of employment.

Paydays

Employees are paid on a weekly basis, resulting in approximately fifty-two (52) paydays every calendar year. Employees are paid every Friday for work completed during the previous pay period. Friendly Fence & Roofing’ official seven-day workweek is from 12:00 a.m. Friday through 11:59 p.m. the following Thursday.

Normally, an employee’s pay is deposited directly into his/her bank account(s). Employees are eligible for direct deposit immediately upon hire, and they sign up for this program through filling out the appropriate paperwork and submitting it to management. Employees may adjust what bank account(s) are being used at any time through a resubmission of the required paperwork. Employees in the direct deposit program receive electronic access to a non-negotiable check stub detailing his/her earnings each payday. For more information, please speak with management.

At times, traditional paper paychecks may be issued to employees for a variety of reasons. These paychecks are normally available by the end of the business day on the relevant payday, and an employee may pick up his/her paycheck at the main office. Unless another pickup method is negotiated by management, only the employee is permitted to pick up his/her paycheck. Your immediate supervisor will inform you if paper paychecks will be issued and will clarify any relevant pickup procedures.

If a payday falls on a holiday, paychecks will be available the business day before the holiday unless Friendly Fence & Roofing specifies otherwise. Under no other circumstances will checks be distributed early.

Employees should verify all paychecks immediately upon receipt. Any employee who feels that his/her paycheck reflects an error should report his/her concerns to his/her supervisor and/or management. Unfortunately, mistakes can occur, and any allegations of a mistake brought to our attention will be promptly investigated and corrected.

Employees who report a mistake in pay or other violations of this policy or who assist in any investigation of violations will not be subject to any form of retaliation.

Company Gas Cards

Based upon business considerations, some employees are issued company gas cards to use for business-related purchases. Company cards may only be used for authorized purchases.

Company gas cards are issued for a specific vehicle. They may only be used to purchase gasoline for the specific vehicle for which they are issued, and the card should be kept in a secure, out-of-sight location in its assigned vehicle.

Employees may NOT use any company card for personal purchases.

Employees are responsible for any cards assigned to them. Lost or stolen cards must be reported to management immediately. Furthermore, use of company cards by individuals other than the assigned employee is forbidden.

Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

Expense Reimbursement

Some employees, through the nature of their work for Friendly Fence & Roofing, may be required to initially pay for certain business-related purchases. Although this is likely to be rare, if it does occur, employees must obtain and submit an itemized receipt to management for reimbursement. Purchases must be pre-approved by management, and all receipts must be turned in no more than one month after the purchase.

If incurred expenses are related to employee travel, additional procedures may apply. Management will communicate additional expectations and procedures to impacted employees prior to any relevant company-related travel.

Failure to follow any policies or procedures related to expense reimbursement may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment.

Access to Personnel Files

Employee files are maintained by management and are considered confidential. Employees of Friendly Fence & Roofing only have access to personnel file information on a need-to-know basis.

Current and former employees wishing to access their own personnel files may do so by contacting Human Resources. Human Resources will generally arrange for a review upon request within 3 days of the request. Personnel files are to be reviewed in the main office at a location provided by management. Employee files may not be taken away from the designated location. Representatives of government or law enforcement agencies, in the course of their duties, may be allowed access to file information.

Employee Image Use

Friendly Fence & Roofing may take photographs and videos during working hours or during work-related functions of any or all employees. Pictures and videos taken of employees while participating in Friendly Fence & Roofing functions remain the property of Friendly Fence & Roofing. As such, these pictures and videos may be used for business-related purposes, including, but not limited to, the company website, social media, marketing, and training materials. Friendly Fence & Roofing is under no obligation to remove any pictures or videos taken of an employee after separation from employment, regardless of whether that separation is initiated by the employee or Friendly Fence & Roofing.

The creation and use of pictures and videos of an employee does not create an employment contract and in no way alter the employment at-will policy of Friendly Fence & Roofing.

Drug-Free and Alcohol-Free Workplace

Although Friendly Fence & Roofing respects an employee’s personal choices with respect to drug and alcohol use, Friendly Fence & Roofing is concerned about the use of these substances, whether on or off the job, if it adversely affects an employee's work performance, efficiency, safety, or health. As a reflection of this concern, Friendly Fence & Roofing has established the following Drug-Free and Alcohol-Free Workplace policy. The following are strictly prohibited by Friendly Fence & Roofing:

Possessing, using, or being under the influence of alcohol, an illegal substance, or a controlled substance during working hours or while driving a company-owned vehicle.

2. Distributing, selling, or purchasing alcohol, an illegal substance, or a controlled substance during working hours or while driving a company-owned vehicle.

Use of prescription and/or over-the-counter drugs may also affect an employee's job performance and ability to perform his/her job safely. If an employee is using a prescription medication or over-the-counter medication in a lawful manner, and that medication does not impact the employee’s ability to safely and effectively perform his/her duties, the previous restrictions do not apply. However, if an employee is using prescription and/or over-the-counter drugs that may impair the employee's ability to safely perform the job or affect the safety or well-being of others, he/she should notify his/her supervisor immediately. An employee may be required to provide a doctor’s verification regarding the employee’s need to take the medication. The employee may be granted a leave of absence for the duration for which he/she will be taking the medication. If available, the employee will be required to use any accrued paid time off (PTO) during this time period. If no paid leave is available, the leave of absence may be granted on an unpaid basis.

Please note: the use of marijuana or its chemical derivatives during work hours has been deemed to be a safety hazard to employees, our customers, and the general public. Its use also negatively impacts our employee’s ability to provide acceptable levels of customer service. For these reasons, even if the use of marijuana is permitted under state or local laws, Friendly Fence & Roofing strictly prohibits the use of marijuana or any of its derivatives during or immediately prior to working hours. Testing positive for marijuana may be considered a violation of this policy, regardless of the employee’s possession of a medical marijuana license or the legal status of recreational use of marijuana.

Violation of this policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

Drug Testing

Each employee, as a condition of employment, will be required to participate in the following types of drug testing:

pre-employment (unless otherwise notified),

reasonable suspicion,

post-accident, and

post-rehabilitation testing.

Any employee who refuses to submit to mandated drug or alcohol test will be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including immediate termination of employment.

Altered samples, substituted samples, and negative dilutes constitute a violation of company policy. Any employee submitting such a sample will be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including immediate termination of employment.

All fees associated with a required drug or alcohol test will be paid by Friendly Fence & Roofing.

When required to take a drug and alcohol test, an employee must sign an Employee Consent Form at the testing facility authorizing the release of testing results to Friendly Fence & Roofing. An employee who refuses to complete the Employee Consent Form will be in violation of this policy, and this violation may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

Unless notified otherwise, testing for the presence of alcohol will be conducted by analysis of breath, and testing for the presence of the metabolites of drugs will be conducted by the analysis of urine.

To ensure the accuracy and fairness of our testing program, all testing will be conducted according to DHHS/SAMHSA guidelines where applicable and will include a screening test; a confirmation test; the opportunity for a split sample; review by a proper official, including the opportunity for employees who test positive to provide a legitimate medical explanation, such as a physician's prescription, for the positive result; and a documented chain of custody.

Reasonable Suspicion Testing

If a supervisor witnesses verifiable evidence that an employee is under the influence of alcohol, controlled substances, or other illegal drugs during work hours or while driving a company-owned vehicle, the employee will be required to submit a urine sample and/or blood sample for substance abuse analysis. Evidence of “under the influence” may include, but is not limited to: slurred speech, uneven gait, mood swings, violent temper, and avoidable accidents involving a vehicle or resulting in property damage.

Post-Accident Testing

After a workplace accident, employees may be required to submit to a drug and alcohol test. For the purposes of this policy, a “workplace accident” shall include any vehicular accidents involving a company-owned vehicle, whether the employee is on-the-clock or not. Furthermore, it will include any vehicular accident when an employee is on-the-clock, even if the employee was driving a personally-owned vehicle. Finally, a “workplace accident” will include all other types of accidents that happen in the course of an employee carrying out his/her duties for Friendly Fence & Roofing.

If a workplace accident occurs, management will analyze the incident to determine if drugs or alcohol could have impacted the incident. This analysis will be made based upon the incident, not the employees involved. All employees involved in the incident will be required to submit to the test, regardless of who was “at fault.”

If management determines that a drug and alcohol test should be performed following an incident, the drug and alcohol test will be completed within a close time proximity to the incident. Involved employees will be informed of the requirement and provided with administrative details regarding obtaining the drug and alcohol test.

Test Results

All drug and alcohol test results will be kept confidential, and only those employees with a bona fide need to know the results will be provided with this information. The employee may submit a written request to receive a copy of his/her substance abuse test results.

An employee may challenge a positive drug or alcohol test by requesting a retest of the sample that tested positive. The employee shall pay all costs of such retest. However, if the retest reverses the results of the initial positive test, Friendly Fence & Roofing shall pay the costs of the retest.

A positive test result to a company-mandated drug and alcohol test may result in disciplinary action, up to and including immediate termination of employment. Friendly Fence & Roofing reserves the right to require, as a condition of reinstatement and continued employment, completion of an approved rehabilitation program, at employee expense, which shall include but not be limited to:

A period of inpatient care

A return to work test prior to reinstatement

Follow-up testing

Any employee testing positive during or subsequent to a rehabilitation program will be subject to immediate termination of employment.

SECTION 2: EMPLOYEE CONDUCT

Customer Service and Ethical Conduct

Customers are the root of what we do – without them, we no longer have a reason or purpose for existing as a company. Ultimately, their satisfaction is what will keep us in business. Even in the middle of unexplained situations that cause customer property damage or would otherwise cause friction, the way we conduct business and the professionalism that we bring to each situation (especially the difficult ones) will have a greater impact on customer satisfaction than any other factor. And, when one customer is satisfied, he/she will let his/her friends and acquaintances know, which will, in turn, help Friendly Fence & Roofing.

The importance of professional conduct when working with our customers cannot be emphasized enough. Because professional conduct is a broad term that is open to many interpretations, we have provided the following guidelines for appropriate conduct:

Company problems may not be discussed with customers. This includes discussing any conflicts between employees and management.

Do not talk negatively about customers, discuss their oddities, or discuss their personal matters, especially in front of other customers or in public.

Providing customer information to anyone who is not an employee is strictly prohibited. This includes other customers, third parties, and individuals of one’s own family.

Borrowing money from a customer is not permitted, nor is trying to sell a customer something that is not company-related (such as Girl Scout cookies).

Friendly Fence & Roofing employees may not solicit customers for charitable donations unless it is part of a management-sanctioned, company-wide charitable drive.

Friendly Fence & Roofing employees may not conduct themselves inappropriately with customers.

Employees should always speak in a professional manner when speaking with customers. Profanity or rude language is strictly prohibited.

Employees may not conduct business with customers outside of official work duties.

In general, ethical behavior is a key element to Friendly Fence & Roofing’ continued success. Each employee must remain committed to certain additional ethical standards and principles while performing his/her job. These include:

Adherence to all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations.

Protection of Friendly Fence & Roofing reputation and assets.

Responsible action that avoids conflicts of interest and other situations potentially harmful to Friendly Fence & Roofing.

Being ethical and honest, including providing truthful information in response to any management inquiry or investigation.

If an employee has any concerns about a customer service situation or how to approach a situation in an ethical manner, he/she should speak with his/her supervisor or another member of management.

Any violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

Prohibited Conduct

Friendly Fence & Roofing considers work rules, guidelines, and work performance important employee responsibilities. They are essential to the proper functioning of our business and ensure that employees work together effectively. When these rules and guidelines are not followed, or an employee's work performance is below Friendly Fence & Roofing standards, disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment, may be taken.

The following is not meant to be a total list of all work rules; they are only examples of the type of conduct that will not be tolerated by Friendly Fence & Roofing. This policy of prohibited conduct does not alter Friendly Fence & Roofing’ policy of at-will employment.

Making false statements or omitting pertinent information on Friendly Fence & Roofing documents, including applications or when responding to management inquiries.

Insubordination: Refusal to obey work orders of supervisors, refusal to perform job assignments, or the use of abusive or threatening language toward a supervisor or member of management.

Bullying: acts or verbal comments that could mentally hurt or isolate a person in the workplace, especially involving repeated incidents or a pattern of behavior that is intended to intimidate, offend, degrade, or humiliate a particular person or group of people. Please note: comments from an employee’s supervisor that are objective and are intended to provide constructive feedback are NOT considered bullying.

Gossiping: discussing another individual’s personal life, particularly when that individual is not an active part of the conversation.

Theft, unauthorized removal, or willful damage of property or resources belonging to Friendly Fence & Roofing, Friendly Fence & Roofing employees, or customers.

Obtaining sales of service or product through false or fraudulent statements to the customer.

Disregard of safety rules and practices and security regulations, including horseplay, wrestling, dangerous practical jokes, or throwing objects.

Possession of dangerous or unauthorized materials, such as explosives or firearms, in the workplace.

Committing any act of violence, threats or intimidation, or fighting.

Using abusive or profane language on Friendly Fence & Roofing or customer premises.

Unauthorized operation of machinery and equipment, or operation of any machinery or equipment that you are not trained and authorized to operate.

Being on Friendly Fence & Roofing or Friendly Fence & Roofing’ customers’ property outside of assigned work duties.

Leaving any workplace, including a jobsite, without properly notifying your supervisor.

Excessive absences or tardiness.

Unacceptable or poor work performance.

Gambling, in any form, on Friendly Fence & Roofing premises.

Littering.

Solicitation of or by employees during working time in the workplace without managerial authorization.

Sleeping or deliberately disregarding assigned work tasks during working hours.

An unacceptable DMV report that changes the insurability status of the employee.

Failure to fully cooperate with any Friendly Fence & Roofing investigation as required by management.

Any conduct that is prohibited by federal, state, or local laws.

Duty to Report

Due to the nature of the business and the liabilities that Friendly Fence & Roofing assumes, an employee has a duty to report to Friendly Fence & Roofing all convictions of or citations for any crime, whether the law violation was federal, state, or local. The following provisions apply to this policy:

Convictions or citations must be reported regardless of the severity of the crime.

Convictions or citations must be reported regardless of whether the violation occurred while the employee was “on-the-clock.”

Field employees must report all traffic violations, whether on Friendly Fence & Roofing or private time, and regardless of their severity.

If an employee is required to maintain a driver’s license as a job requirement, he/she must report to Friendly Fence & Roofing if his/her driver’s license is revoked.

An employee must report knowledge of a warrant being issued for his/her arrest.

An employee must report any civil lawsuits filed against him/her.

Failure to report convictions, citations, or warrants may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment. At Friendly Fence & Roofing’ discretion, violation of federal, state, or local laws may also result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

Prohibition Against Harassment

It is Friendly Fence & Roofing’ policy to ensure that its employees have a workplace free of sexual and other types of harassment. Harassment based upon membership or perceived membership in any protected class is strictly prohibited by Friendly Fence & Roofing. This prohibition includes inappropriate actions and statements made by management, supervisors, employees, and nonemployees who are present in the workplace. Friendly Fence & Roofing will take all steps necessary to prevent and eliminate unlawful harassment.

Furthermore, any employee who places a complaint about sexual or other harassment in the workplace will not be retaliated against for lodging that complaint. Furthermore, retaliation against individuals for cooperating with an investigation of a harassment complaint is unlawful and will not be tolerated.

Definition of Prohibited Harassment

Prohibited harassment is conduct that, because of the individual’s membership in a protected class,:

has the purpose or effect of creating an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment;

has the purpose or effect of substantially and unreasonably interfering with an individual’s work performance; or

otherwise adversely affects an individual’s employment opportunities.

Prohibited harassment includes, but is not limited to, epithets; slurs; jokes; pranks; innuendo; comments; written or graphic material; stereotyping; or other threatening, hostile, or intimidating acts based on membership in a protected class as outlined by local, state, or federal laws.

Definition of Sexual Harassment.

While all forms of harassment are prohibited, sexual harassment is further outlined by additional laws. “Sexual harassment” is generally defined under law as unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favors, and other verbal or physical conduct of a sexual nature where:

Submission to or rejection of such conduct is made either explicitly or implicitly a term or condition of any individual’s employment or as a basis for employment decisions; or

Such conduct has the purpose or effect of unreasonably interfering with an individual’s work performance or creating an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment.

Below are some examples of conduct that, if unwelcome, may constitute sexual harassment (Please note: this list should not be considered exhaustive):

Unwanted sexual advances, whether they involve physical touching or not;

Sexual epithets, jokes, written or oral references to sexual conduct, gossip regarding one’s sex life, comments about an individual’s body, comments about an individual’s sexual activity, deficiencies, or prowess;

Displaying sexually suggestive objects, pictures, or cartoons;

Unwelcome leering, whistling, brushing up against the body, sexual gestures, or suggestive or insulting comments;

Inquiries into one’s sexual experiences; and

Discussion of one’s sexual activities.

Sexual harassment (and other forms of harassment) can occur between any individuals, regardless of each person’s sex, gender, or other membership in a protected class. It can also occur regardless of each individual’s position within the organization or related to the other individual. Harassers can be a superior, subordinate, co-worker, or anyone in the workplace, including an independent contractor, temporary employee, vendor, customer, or visitor.

Furthermore, sexual harassment can occur both inside and outside the immediate work environment or workday. Harassment can occur while employees are traveling for business or at company-sponsored events or parties. In addition, calls, texts, emails, and social media usage by employees can constitute unlawful harassment, even if they occur away from the workplace, on personal devices, or during non-work hours.

Complaint Procedure

Any employee who believes he/she has been subject to or witnessed illegal discrimination, including sexual or other forms of unlawful harassment, should file a complaint following the procedures outlined in the “Complaint Reporting Procedure” policy presented in Section 1 of this handbook. All complaints will be investigated promptly and, to the extent possible, with regard for confidentiality.

Fraternization

Relatives may be hired by the company if the new employee will not work as a direct supervisor or subordinate of the existing employee and the employment will not cause either favoritism or the appearance of favoritism between the existing and new employee. For the purposes of this policy, “relatives” are defined as spouses, domestic partners, children, siblings, parents, or grandparents.

While Friendly Fence & Roofing has no desire to interfere with the private lives of its employees or their off duty conduct, Friendly Fence & Roofing prohibits employees from dating any direct subordinates. Furthermore, Friendly Fence & Roofing will consider it a violation of this policy if a personal relationship with another employee interferes with an employee’s ability to effectively complete his/her assigned tasks or if the relationship causes a conflict of interests for either employee.

If a romantic relationship were to develop between two existing employees, the employees are required to immediately notify their direct supervisors regarding the existence of said relationship. Where such conduct impacts the work environment in a negative manner, Friendly Fence & Roofing reserves the right to take whatever action is appropriate, in its discretion, to protect Friendly Fence & Roofing’ interest. This may include transfer of one or both parties from a department, reassignment of position, or other action up to and including termination of employment.

Conflicts of Interest

Friendly Fence & Roofing expects all employees to conduct themselves and company business with the highest ethical standards in addition to adhering to all federal, state, and local laws and regulations. Although Friendly Fence & Roofing recognizes and respects an employee’s right to engage in activities outside of employment, adhering to the highest ethical standards includes, among other things, avoiding real and potential conflicts of interests in both workplace and personal time.

A conflict of interest exists when an employee’s loyalties or actions are divided between Friendly Fence & Roofing’ interests and those of another person or entity, such as a competitor, supplier, or customer. An employee who is unsure as to whether a certain situation constitutes a conflict of interest or the appearance of a conflict of interest should discuss the situation with his/her immediate supervisor or management for clarification.

It is not possible to define all the situations that might create a conflict of interest. The list below suggests some types of activity that indicate a conflict of interest resulting in improper behavior, unacceptable personal integrity, or unacceptable ethics:

Simultaneous ownership of, management of, or employment by another company that is a competitor of Friendly Fence & Roofing.

Being an owner, manager, or employee of a company that is a Friendly Fence & Roofing supplier or vendor.

Engaging in “side work,” “moon-lighting,” or self-employment while employed by Friendly Fence & Roofing.

Using company assets, such as company-owned computers, or labor for personal gain.

Having a direct or indirect financial interest in or relationship with a competitor, customer, or supplier, except that ownership of less than 1% of the publicly traded stock of a corporation will not be considered a conflict.

Borrowing money from customers or companies, other than recognized loan institutions, from which our company buys services, materials, equipment, or supplies.

Accepting gifts or entertainment in excess of $25 in value from an outside organization or agency.

Committing Friendly Fence & Roofing to give its financial or other support to any outside activity or organization except within the ordinary course and scope of employment.

Participating in civic or professional organization activities in a manner that divulges confidential company information.

Misusing privileged information or revealing confidential data, including customer information, to individuals not employed by Friendly Fence & Roofing.

Using one’s position in the company or knowledge of its affairs for personal gains.

Developing a personal relationship with another employee of Friendly Fence & Roofing that might interfere with the exercise of impartial judgment in decisions affecting Friendly Fence & Roofing or any employees of Friendly Fence & Roofing.

Engaging in practices or procedures that violate antitrust laws, commercial bribery laws, copyright laws, discrimination laws, campaign contribution laws, or other laws regulating the conduct of company business.

Please note: it is not a conflict of interest to engage in protected concerted activity that includes joining with other employees for your mutual aid and protection. Nothing in this policy should be interpreted to limit an employee’s rights under the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA).

Confidentiality and Trade Secrets

As a condition of initial and continued employment with Friendly Fence & Roofing, all current employees are expected to protect and preserve Friendly Fence & Roofing’ proprietary, confidential, and trade secret information. This information is valuable to all employees, as it is what helps our company stay in business. Furthermore, former employees are reminded that proprietary, confidential, and trade secret information is protected under federal and state laws, and Friendly Fence & Roofing may take any and all legal means available to protect its trade secrets. "Trade secret" means information, including a formula, pattern, compilation, program, device, method, technique, or process, that:

Derives independent economic value, actual or potential, from not being generally known to the public or to other persons who can obtain economic value from its disclosure or use; and

Is the subject of efforts that are reasonable under the circumstances to maintain its secrecy.

The following are examples of trade secret information that is protected by this policy and related laws:

Marketing concepts, labor and material costs, and pricing methods of Friendly Fence & Roofing.

The contents of private written or oral contracts or understandings between Friendly Fence & Roofing and a third party, including customers, suppliers, and vendors.

The details of any statistical data, training manuals, financial statements, forms, techniques, methods, or procedures not generally known to competitors of Friendly Fence & Roofing.

Long-range plans, budgets, acquisition strategies, methods of operations, and financial performance belonging to Friendly Fence & Roofing and not generally known to the public.

Names and addresses and any related information pertaining to Friendly Fence & Roofing’ customers that are not generally known to the public.

Confidential employee information, such as medical information, performance review details, and social security numbers.

All Information protected by the Uniform Trade Secrets Act and any state version thereof.

An employee who improperly uses or discloses trade secrets or confidential business information will be subject to disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment and legal action, even if he/she does not actually benefit from the disclosed information. In the event that an employee is terminated or voluntarily resigns from their position with Friendly Fence & Roofing, this information must remain confidential for a period of twelve (12) months following the date of departure.

If an employee is approached by an individual representing either law enforcement or the media requesting information, he/she should refer all inquiries to Friendly Fence & Roofing ownership.

Employees are not prohibited by this policy from engaging in activities for their mutual aid and protection. Employees have the right, without violating this policy, to discuss among themselves issues relevant to their pay, benefits, and working conditions, or otherwise legally engage in concerted activity.

Security

The security of our office, company-owned vehicles, and worksites, as well as the welfare of our employees, requires that every individual be constantly aware of potential security risks. You should immediately notify your supervisor if you notice persons acting in a suspicious manner in any workspace, or when keys are lost or misplaced.

Employees entrusted with keys to the office, other company facilities, and company-owned vehicles are responsible for the safekeeping of the keys and the security and protection of company property. This includes any time the employee is present, regardless of whether the office is closed or customers are present.

Furthermore, employees are responsible for the security of company-owned vehicles assigned to them at all times. Although we realize that some things are out of an employee’s control, an employee is responsible for taking all prudent and responsible actions to ensure the security of company property, including ensuring that all company vehicle doors are closed and locked at all times when the employee is not present.

Workplace Violence Prevention

Friendly Fence & Roofing is committed to providing a safe, violence-free workplace for our employees. Because of this commitment, Friendly Fence & Roofing strictly prohibits and will not tolerate any act of aggression or violence made toward or by any employee.

An act of aggression may include, but is not limited to:

any verbal or physical harassment or abuse,

attempts to intimidate others,

menacing gestures,

stalking,

or any other hostile, aggressive, and/or destructive actions taken for the purposes of intimidation.

This policy applies to all work sites, including customer property and the main office, as well as all company-sponsored functions.

All employees are considered responsible for keeping our work environment free from violence or potential violence. Although management discourages employees from engaging in any physical confrontation with a violent or potentially violent individual, employees are encouraged to take actions necessary to ensure their safety.

If a threat is imminently dangerous, the employee should immediately contact law enforcement and emergency services. In addition, all employees who witness or are the recipients of violent behavior should promptly inform their supervisor. All threats will be promptly investigated, and any individual engaging in violence against the company, its employees, or its property will be prosecuted to the full extent of the law. No employee will be subject to retaliation, intimidation, or discipline as a result of reporting a threat in good faith under this policy.

Firearms and weapons cannot be brought into the workplace at any time. Friendly Fence & Roofing’ workplace includes all offices, warehouses, workshops, company-owned vehicles, Friendly Fence & Roofing’ customers’ property, and any other location in which Friendly Fence & Roofing business is conducted.

In addition, any violations of this policy by an employee may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

Commitment to Safety

Protecting the safety of our employees and visitors is highly important to Friendly Fence & Roofing. All employees have the responsibility to ensure a safe working environment by following all safety guidelines, using commonsense rules and safe practices, and by notifying management when any health or safety issues are present. In the event of an emergency, notify the appropriate emergency personnel and management immediately.

Furthermore, employees are required to report any work-related injury or illness, no matter how small, to their immediate supervisor. With the assistance of the employee’s supervisor (if necessary), the employee will complete all required incident reporting forms, including all necessary forms for Worker’s Compensation filing. The employee will be kept informed at all stages of the Worker’s Compensation process in accordance with any related laws.

Attendance, Absence, and Punctuality

Based on the needs of Friendly Fence & Roofing and its customers, each employee is expected to be present at work for all of his/her scheduled hours on a consistent basis. These hours are scheduled based upon Friendly Fence & Roofing’ expected call volume, and any deviations from the schedule result in hardship for our customers and other employees. This should be avoided in most circumstances.

Friendly Fence & Roofing expects each employee to report to work prepared to start work. Employees are also expected to remain at work for their entire work schedule, except for meal periods or when required to leave on Friendly Fence & Roofing authorized business. Late arrival, early departure, or other absences from scheduled hours are disruptive and must be avoided.

If an employee anticipates being late for work, the employee must notify his/her supervisor at least 30 minutes before the start of his/her scheduled work time. For any absence that was not pre-approved, the employee must notify Friendly Fence & Roofing of his/her continued absence each day he/she is absent unless an emergency prevents such notification. Management recommends that employees provide their supervisors with an honest reason or explanation for any absence not pre-approved. To obtain pre-approval for any leave of absence, including vacation, an employee should submit a leave request to his/her immediate supervisor for approval at least two weeks prior to the scheduled leave date.

An employee who does not call or report to work for three consecutive workdays will be considered to have voluntarily resigned employment with Friendly Fence & Roofing, unless there are extenuating circumstances. Supervisors experiencing such absences should contact management immediately.

Please note: excessive absenteeism or tardiness (excused or unexcused) will not be tolerated. Excessive absenteeism may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

Professional Appearance and Uniforms

Each employee is a representative of Friendly Fence & Roofing in the eyes of our customers and the public, so it is important that all personnel dress in a professional manner while working. Being dressed in a professional manner includes appropriate dress, as outlined below, proper hygiene, and being properly groomed. Employees who report to work inappropriately dressed or groomed may be asked, among other options, to leave and return in acceptable attire.

Employees are expected to wear the provided uniform shirts, sweatshirts, and jackets specific to the brand. Personnel are expected to provide their own pants, belts, and professional shoes/boots as required components of the Friendly Fence & Roofing uniform. The following provisions apply to employee-provided uniform components:

Pants/shorts must be neat, in good repair, and be business casual (e.g., slacks) in style. Jeans, athletic wear, and other casual styles are not considered acceptable without specific managerial authorization.

Pants/shorts must be black or khaki in color.

Belts and footwear must be neutral in color.

Footwear must be closed-toe and professional in style, and are protectant of being on work site, Athletic shoes are not considered acceptable.

All clothing worn must be of a cut and style that is appropriate to the work environment. Please note: employees are prohibited from wearing items of clothing that display sexual or other potentially offensive statements, logos, or designs at any time while representing Friendly Fence & Roofing, driving company-owned vehicles, or on Friendly Fence & Roofing property. Management reserves the final authority to determine what articles of clothing do not meet these standards for professionalism.

Employees must wear the required uniforms at any time while representing Friendly Fence & Roofing. This includes any time while on-the clock, such as normal working hours, responding on-call, and representing Friendly Fence & Roofing in other locations (e.g., training seminars). Please contact your supervisor if you have questions as to what constitutes appropriate attire for a given situation.

Uniforms must be neat and in good repair at all times. Stains; tears; missing buttons, patches, and pockets; and other damage will not be tolerated. Informal inspections will occur on an ongoing basis, and any deficiencies will result in the employee being asked to change. Replacement uniform pieces will be provided by Friendly Fence & Roofing as needed. Although Friendly Fence & Roofing understands that some damage as a result of wear and tear will occur, misconduct or unreasonable wear and tear on the uniform may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment. Disciplinary action may include the employee being required to pay for replacement pieces. Final determination between normal wear and misconduct/unreasonable wear and tear will be made by management.

Cleaning and costs associated with cleaning are solely the employee’s responsibility. Each employee has the option of having his/her uniforms laundered and cared for however and wherever he/she sees fit.

Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

Smoking and Tobacco Use

Although Friendly Fence & Roofing does not take employment action based upon an employee’s choices during his/her personal time, smoking and using other tobacco-based products while on the clock or in Friendly Fence & Roofing’ uniform can have a significant impact on Friendly Fence & Roofing, its customers, and its other employees. Because of this, smoking or using other tobacco-based products by Friendly Fence & Roofing employees during work hours, in Friendly Fence & Roofing uniform, or while otherwise representing Friendly Fence & Roofing is governed by the following rules:

Smoking and tobacco use at the main office location must be conducted outside of the building and away from any entrances and open windows. Smoking and tobacco use are strictly prohibited in all facilities, including all warehouses.

Littering will not be tolerated. Employees must properly dispose of all smoking or tobacco product-related trash.

Smoking and use of tobacco products is strictly prohibited in Friendly Fence & Roofing-owned vehicles.

Employees are prohibited from smoking on customers’ property.

All above regulations apply equally to all types of smoking, including traditional cigarettes, electronic cigarettes, cigars, pipes, and other smoking products.

Smoking and using other tobacco products while in uniform can impact our company's image in our customers' eyes. If Friendly Fence & Roofing receives a complaint from a customer regarding a tobacco or smoke-related odor in his/her home because of an employee, it will be considered a violation of this policy.

Violations of this policy will result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

Vehicles

Personal Vehicles

Friendly Fence & Roofing provides a parking lot at the main office location for employees’ personal vehicles. Employees are prohibited from parking vehicles in the company parking lot that are not in working condition. Furthermore, employees must follow all laws concerning safe parking in the office parking lot. Failure to do so will be considered a violation of this policy, and Friendly Fence & Roofing reserves the right to contact either local law enforcement or have a vehicle towed at employee expense.

Friendly Fence & Roofing is not responsible for any loss to, damage to, or theft from your personal vehicle at any time, including while parked on company premises. Therefore, we recommend all unattended personal vehicles are locked and valuables are removed from sight.

Company-Owned Vehicles

Certain employees of Friendly Fence & Roofing will be required to operate vehicles as a mandatory job function. To facilitate the employee’s successful completion of mandatory job functions, Friendly Fence & Roofing owns a number of vehicles for these employees to use. The following provisions apply employee use of these company-owned vehicles:

Based upon certain factors, such as but not limited to job description, Friendly Fence & Roofing has instituted a vehicle take-home benefit program. When this program applies, an employee is permitted to drive his/her assigned company vehicle to the employee's home at the end of his/her shift.

Company-owned vehicles are for employee use only. Individuals who are not Friendly Fence & Roofing employees are strictly prohibited from riding in company-owned vehicles at any time. This includes, but is not limited to, an employee’s spouse, children, and any other dependents.

Employees are responsible for ensuring that his/her assigned vehicle is maintained in a clean, stocked, and organized manner.

Employees are responsible for tracking the mileage in his/her assigned vehicle. When the employee’s assigned vehicle is due for maintenance, such as an oil change, the employee is responsible for notifying management. Employees will be given a specific schedule of maintenance for the vehicle he/she is assigned in a separate document.

Management must be notified in the event that a vehicle may need repair or maintenance outside of the regular scheduled maintenance (e.g., abnormal noises, broken windshield).

Traffic Violations and Insurability

In addition, specific Friendly Fence & Roofing employees are required, as a condition of employment with Friendly Fence & Roofing, to maintain a valid state driver's license. For these employees, any traffic violations must be reported immediately to management, even if that violation occurs when an employee is not working and driving his/her personal vehicle. Any traffic violations or revocations of a driver's license that result in Friendly Fence & Roofing vehicle insurance rate increases or an inability to insure a specific employee may result in disciplinary action, including job reassignment or termination, as determined by management.

Due to both customer service implications and safety concerns, employees must follow all traffic laws and safe driving techniques at all times. Speeding, running red lights or stop signs, unsafe lane changes, and other inappropriate driving actions are incredibly dangerous, and they reflect poorly on Friendly Fence & Roofing’ image within the community and potential customer base. As a result, these behaviors are strictly prohibited. Employees will be financially responsible for all traffic fines incurred, regardless of whether they are driving Friendly Fence & Roofing-owned vehicles or personally-owned vehicles on company time.

Furthermore, all employees of Friendly Fence & Roofing are required to wear seatbelts at all times while driving Friendly Fence & Roofing-owned vehicles or on company time. Failure to do so will be considered a violation of this policy.

If an employee is involved in a vehicular accident in either a company-owned vehicle or on company time, the following regulations apply:

The accident must be reported immediately to management, regardless of time of day. At management’s discretion, management may respond to the scene of the accident immediately, regardless of time of day, in order to make sure that proper company procedures are followed.

The employee will be required to immediately call the local police department, regardless of the severity of the accident or the individual suspected to be "at fault" for the accident.

If Friendly Fence & Roofing determines that damage to a company vehicle was the result of a violation of any company policy or traffic law, it may result in disciplinary action against the employee.

If damage to a company-owned vehicle is the result of an employee’s negligent or criminal behavior, the employee may be held liable for any deductibles associated with repairing company-owned vehicle.

Violations of any aspect of this vehicle policy will result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

Business Telephones

Friendly Fence & Roofing maintains company telephones at its main office location. These lines are for the benefit of our customers, suppliers, and business associates. Employees are expected to answer all phones rapidly and in accordance with all procedures presented. To help ensure that our employees are representing our company effectively, all telephone calls to our main business lines will be recorded.

Management understands that employees may need to occasionally make personal telephone calls using the business telephones. Although employees are allowed to use the business lines for personal purposes when workload permits, lengthy or frequent calls are prohibited. If personal calls interfere with an employee’s productivity or the functioning of company business, disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment, may be taken.

Mobile Electronic Devices

Please note: employees who are in violation of all provisions listed in this policy may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment. Disciplinary action may, at the discretion of management, include financial responsibility for damage or replacement of a company-owned device if it is determined that damage or loss of a mobile device is the result of negligence.

Cellular Telephones

Based upon business-related reasons, such as job description, Friendly Fence & Roofing requires specific employees to provide personally-owned cellular telephones for business purposes. Management may further require that personally-owned cellular telephones or plans meet specific requirements.

When an employee is required to provide his/her own cellular telephone, he/she must keep it with him/her at all times while working or on-call. While working or on-call, all business-related calls must be answered immediately unless a safety or customer service conflict is present. Any missed calls must be returned as soon as the initial conflict is resolved.

Even when not required for business-related purposes, personal cell phones may be kept on an employee’s person during work hours. However, if management finds that excessive personal calls are interfering with Friendly Fence & Roofing work, it will be considered a violation of this policy.

Company Provided Tablets
