All company-owned tablets are intended for business use, and the employee must keep it with him/her at all times while working or on-call. However, as assigned tablets are NOT intended for personal use, any personal use of tablets will be considered a violation of this policy.

Downloading unauthorized applications onto tablets owned by Friendly Fence & Roofing, regardless of the application’s type or function, is strictly prohibited. Employees who wish to download a business-related application should ask management for permission. Permission will only be granted after management establishes that the application is safe and business-related.

If management requires certain applications be downloaded for business reasons, management will inform employees regarding any necessary procedures related to the download process.

Electronic Device Use and Vehicles

Employees are prohibited from using certain cell phone functions while operating any motor vehicle on Friendly Fence & Roofing business. The prohibited functions include hand-held calls and text messaging (both sending and receiving), as well as all other functions not utilizing a hands-free device. Employees are permitted to use hands-free devices while driving, but they are encouraged to stop in a safe location (e.g., parking lot) before completing any lengthy calls.

Employees are strictly prohibited from using tablets in any way other than hands-free navigation while operating a motor vehicle.

For the purposes of this policy, "operating a motor vehicle" shall include any time a vehicle is within the flow of traffic, including while stopped at a stop sign or red traffic light. In addition, any vehicle operated for Friendly Fence & Roofing purposes or while you are "on the clock" is included in this policy, regardless of whether the vehicle is Friendly Fence & Roofing-owned or your personal vehicle. The one and only exception is contacting emergency services.

Furthermore, these prohibitions apply to all electronic devices, whether they are company-owned or personally-owned.

Violations of any aspect of this policy will result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

Computers, Internet, Email, and Other Resources

Friendly Fence & Roofing provides its employees with a wide variety of communication tools to assist them in effectively completing their work tasks. These resources may include, but are not limited to, computers, faxing, scanners, Internet, intranet, and email. All communication using these tools should be handled in a professional and respectful manner.

All computers and systems, including email, are considered company property. Because of this, employees do not have a right to privacy in their use of these tools. All company property and communications made using company-provided equipment or services are subject to inspection by the company at any time, with or without notice. In addition, even after an email, voicemail, or other communication is deleted, a copy may still be on the company’s systems. Finally, all emails and other forms of stored communication are considered business records. All business records may be subject to federal and state recordkeeping requirements, and they may be needed in the event of a lawsuit involving the company.

All passwords and security codes involving technological equipment remain the property of Friendly Fence & Roofing. Employees are forbidden from changing any passwords or codes without managerial authorization, and the employee must immediately provide any new passwords or codes to management after they have been created.

Friendly Fence & Roofing purchases or licenses the use of various computer software programs. Neither Friendly Fence & Roofing nor any of Friendly Fence & Roofing’ employees has the right to duplicate this computer software or its related documentation. Friendly Fence & Roofing does not condone the illegal duplication of software. You must use the software in accordance with the license agreement. This policy applies not only to individual desktop computers and laptops, but to local area networks as well.

Employees should keep in mind that information transmitted through email and the internet may contain viruses or malware, and information an employee transmits and receives on company property could damage the company’s property, as well as the reputation and/or competitiveness of Friendly Fence & Roofing. To protect against possible problems, employees must be vigilant for risky communication from unknown senders and advertisers. When confronted with suspicious communications, employees should bring it to the attention of management prior to opening the communication and any attachments. It also is against company policy to turn off antivirus protection software or make unauthorized changes to system configurations installed on company computers.

Accessing pornographic, offensive, or other inappropriate information in violation of Friendly Fence & Roofing policy is expressly prohibited. This prohibition includes, but is not limited to:

Use of personal equipment while on-the-clock.

Use of personal equipment while on company or customer property, including company-owned vehicles, regardless of whether on or off the clock.

Use of company-owned equipment, including cell phones, tablets, and computers, regardless of whether on or off the clock.

Please note: all policies and procedures of Friendly Fence & Roofing apply to all of an employee’s work-related behavior, including use of email and the internet. Violations of any company policy, including harassment, customer service, and trade secrets policies related to electronic communication will be investigated and may be considered a violation of both this policy and any other relevant policies.

Employees are required to immediately report loss of any company-owned devices or computers, compromised passwords, or devices that are not functioning properly. Failure to report lost or potentially compromised equipment will be considered a violation of this policy.

Nothing in this policy is designed to interfere with, restrain, or prevent employee communications regarding wages, hours, or other terms and conditions of employment as protected under the National Labor Relations Act. Employees have the right to engage in or refrain from such activities.

Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

Use of Company Property

Friendly Fence & Roofing provides furniture, desks, storage areas, work areas, and other Friendly Fence & Roofing-provided equipment/facilities. These assets are referred to collectively as “Friendly Fence & Roofing assets.” These Friendly Fence & Roofing assets are provided to employees at Friendly Fence & Roofing’ expense to assist you in carrying out Friendly Fence & Roofing business.

Friendly Fence & Roofing reserves the right to inspect any employee's work area, assigned company-owned vehicle, locker, desk, or any other enclosed container kept by the employee on the work premises or in a company vehicle. Friendly Fence & Roofing also reserves the right to inspect all belongings of employees on its premises, including packages, briefcases, purses and handbags, gym bags, and personal vehicles on company property. Such inspection may be done with or without notice and with or without cause. Friendly Fence & Roofing may choose to remove all company property and other items that are in violation of Company rules and policies that are discovered through any such inspection.

If the employee has a lock on a storage area, the employee shall open the area upon request. Failure to unlock a storage area shall be deemed an act of gross insubordination and shall be grounds for immediate termination.

Items or information of a personal nature may be discovered in the course of any inspection conducted in accordance with the exercise of Friendly Fence & Roofing’ rights if you use Friendly Fence & Roofing assets for personal purposes. You consent to such access by accepting and using Friendly Fence & Roofing assets.

Furthermore, all documentation related to business processes and responses to customer calls for service are considered Friendly Fence & Roofing property. As such, this property may not be used by employees for their personal gain. For the purposes of this policy, photographs taken during calls for service are included within the scope of "documentation."

Friendly Fence & Roofing property may not be removed from Friendly Fence & Roofing premises without the proper authorization of management. If an employee loses, breaks, or damages any property, he/she should report it to his/her supervisor immediately.

Failure to respect Friendly Fence & Roofing property and use it with due care will result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment. Failure to use assets with proper care may be considered a violation regardless of whether damage to assets occur.

Social Media

Note: As used in this policy, “social media” refers to blogs, forums, and social networking sites, such as Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, YouTube, Instagram, and SnapChat.

On-duty Use of Social Media

Unless use of social media is required as part of an employee’s job duties, employees are prohibited from engaging in social media use while working or on company-owned equipment. Employees are reminded that all company-owned and provided equipment remains company property, and Friendly Fence & Roofing has the ability and right to monitor all use of company-owned equipment.

Off-the-Clock Use of Social Media

Friendly Fence & Roofing does not prohibit employees from maintaining personal websites, social media accounts, or weblogs on their own time using their own devices. However, employees must ensure that social media activity does not interfere with their ability to work. In general, Friendly Fence & Roofing considers social media activities to be personal endeavors, and employees may use them to express their thoughts or promote their ideas.

Although Friendly Fence & Roofing does not prohibit social media use during personal time on personally-owned equipment, the following conduct is prohibited:

Knowingly making false statements that are intended solely to harm the reputation of Friendly Fence & Roofing products, services, employees, managers, supervisors, senior management, officers, and/or owners.

Disclosing Friendly Fence & Roofing’ trade secrets or other confidential proprietary information, including private and/or personal information, related to customers, vendors, employees, supervisors, managers, or owners.

Using social media in a way that creates a conflict of interest, such as placing false reviews of either Friendly Fence & Roofing or its competitors, or advertising for a competitor.

Making discriminatory or harassing comments that violate federal, state, or local laws or are otherwise prohibited by Friendly Fence & Roofing’ Prohibition Against Harassment policy.

Making threats to any customer, vendor, employee, manager, or owner, including threats concerning their respective family members or personal property.

Posting images, including photographs or drawings, depicting the confidential, personal, and/or health-related information of our customers.

Making an endorsement in support of Friendly Fence & Roofing, its products or services, even if using a personal account, without disclosing your relationship with Friendly Fence & Roofing.

If an employee identifies his/herself as an employee of Friendly Fence & Roofing, he/she must ensure his/her profile and related content is an accurate and fair representation of his/her relationship with Friendly Fence & Roofing.

Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including immediate termination of employment.

Social Media Conduct Post-Employment

Employees must ensure that their social media activity does not interfere with their ability to perform their job duties. If an employee is terminated or voluntarily resigns from their position with Friendly Fence & Roofing, the terms regarding responsible social media posting and the protection of company-related content shall remain in effect for a period of twelve (12) months following their departure. Any violation of these terms, including the disclosure of confidential or proprietary information, may result in legal action.

Note: Nothing in this policy is meant to, nor should it be interpreted to, in any way limit your rights under any applicable federal, state, or local laws, including your rights under the National Labor Relations Act to engage in protected concerted activities with other employees to improve or discuss terms and conditions of employment, such as wages, working conditions, and benefits.

SECTION 3: EMPLOYEE BENEFITS

Paid Time Off (PTO)

Friendly Fence & Roofing provides paid time off (PTO) to all employees. PTO may be used for any personal need, including family emergencies, illnesses, and vacations.

PTO accrual occurs immediately upon hire; however, a new employee is ineligible to use his/her PTO until he/she has completed the company waiting period.

Part-time employees will accrue time in accordance with a separate agreement with management.

Each eligible full-time employee accrues 6.7 hours of PTO each month, resulting in approximately 80 hours of PTO each year. If PTO is not used within the year time frame, the accrued PTO will be forfeited.

An employee’s pay while using PTO will be based upon the employee’s pay agreement with Friendly Fence & Roofing at the time of the leave. Please refer to that document or speak with management for more information.

PTO may NOT be taken until after it has been accrued. Employees will not be permitted to carry a negative PTO balance. If an employee does not have enough accrued PTO to address a request or unplanned emergency, he/she should speak with management regarding unpaid leave.

In addition, employees are required to use accrued but unused PTO for any absences. Management will only consider unpaid leave when all PTO has been used or under extreme and rare circumstances.

PTO may be taken in 4-hour increments.

When an employee wishes to use PTO for a known, planned event (e.g., vacations), he/she must submit a leave request to management for approval. Pre-approval from management is required for any event that may be logically planned in advance. Scheduling, including planned leaves, is normally performed at least 2 weeks in advance, and all requests for PTO should be submitted prior to this time. You are encouraged to submit your request early. Management will consider all PTO requests based upon business necessity, and management will grant all PTO requests that will not significantly hinder the company’s ability to meet those needs. PTO requests may be denied based upon business necessity at any time.

In the event that you and another employee select the same time for your planned PTO and both of you cannot be off at the same time, day the request was made will be the determining factor. If both employees requested the leave on the same day, length of service will be the determining factor.

Unplanned PTO, such as to address an illness, does not need prior approval; however, it must represent an urgent, unforeseen need. The employee should disclose the reason for the unplanned leave to management when placing the request. Management retains the right to request any employee to verify the need for leave because of an illness or injury with a written statement from a physician. Although management may waive the requirement in certain circumstances, employees are required to provide a release from a physician to return to work after an absence of 3 days or longer.

If an employee becomes sick during the day, his/her supervisor must be notified before the employee leaves the work site.

For any absence that was not pre-approved, the employee must notify Friendly Fence & Roofing of his/her continued absence each day he/she is absent unless an emergency prevents such notification.

Employees will NOT receive payment for any accrued but unused PTO upon separation from employment.

Holidays

Friendly Fence & Roofing observes 6 paid holidays per year. Friendly Fence & Roofing paid holidays include:

New Year's Day (January 1)

Memorial Day (Last Monday in May)

Independence Day (July 4)

Labor Day (First Monday in September)

Thanksgiving Day (Fourth Thursday in November)

Christmas Day (December 25)

If an employee wishes to observe a religious holiday that is not already scheduled by Friendly Fence & Roofing, he/she should speak with his/her supervisor regarding transferring holiday pay from a normally scheduled holiday, use of PTO, or unpaid leave. In accordance with business necessity, Friendly Fence & Roofing will seek to reasonably accommodate individuals’ religious observances.

Regular full-time employees who have completed the company waiting period receive pay for holidays in accordance with their pay plan. Employees should refer to his/her pay plan document or speak with management for more information. Full-time employees will not receive holiday pay before completing the company waiting period. Part-time employees are not eligible for holiday pay.

Unless dictated otherwise by state or federal law, an employee is ineligible for holiday pay if he/she has an unexcused absence on the workday immediately prior or after a holiday. To retain eligibility for holiday pay, an employee who becomes ill or injured and is unable to work one of these days must confirm the need to be away from work through submitting a doctor’s note. An employee retains eligibility for holiday pay if a holiday falls during approved pre-planned PTO. An employee will NOT receive holiday pay if he/she is on an unpaid leave of absence.

If a holiday falls on a weekend, it will normally be observed on the closest normal business day. However, Friendly Fence & Roofing may close on another day, grant holiday pay in lieu of closing on any day, or grant a floating day off instead of closing. Employees will be notified of relevant procedures prior to any weekend holiday.

Please note: holiday benefit hours are NOT considered "hours worked" for the purposes of establishing an employee’s standard rate of pay or hours worked for overtime.

Crime Victims’ Leave

Friendly Fence & Roofing grants unpaid leave to an employee if he/she or a member of his/her immediate family is the victim of a crime. This leave may be used to prepare for and/or attend court proceedings related to the crime. Please note: employees who are charged with a crime are not eligible for Crime Victims’ Leave. Friendly Fence & Roofing may, at its discretion, require documentation supporting the employee’s need for Crime Victims’ Leave. Crime Victims’ Leave is an unpaid leave; however, an employee may choose to use any accrued but unused paid time off during this otherwise unpaid leave.

Unpaid Leaves of Absence

Friendly Fence & Roofing may grant a personal unpaid leave of absence based upon specific circumstances. Unpaid leaves of absence are normally reserved for extended leaves in excess of two weeks. Requests for personal leaves of absence should be limited to unusual circumstances. Employees are required to use any available PTO before beginning an unpaid leave of absence.

In some cases of illness or injury, an extended unpaid leave of absence may be governed by federal, state, or local laws. Friendly Fence & Roofing will grant leaves in accordance with any relevant laws.

Unpaid leaves of absence may impact an employee’s eligibility for other employee benefits. Management will discuss any impact with an employee when discussing approval of an extended leave. Friendly Fence & Roofing will not pay the Health Care premiums of any employee or, if applicable, an employee’s dependents during an extended leave of absence unless such payment is required by state or federal law.

Employees should refer to the below “Return to Work” policy for more information following an extended leave of absence for medical purposes.

Return to Work

Unless informed otherwise by management, employees are required to submit the treating physician’s release before returning to work after any medically related leave of absence of 3 days or longer. This requirement includes workplace accidents. This release must detail any medically advised restrictions based upon the doctor’s analysis of the employee’s abilities and job duties.

Because employees may lose eligibility for many benefits, including medical insurance, if they are away from the workplace for extended periods, employees are strongly encouraged to return to work as soon as possible.

If an employee’s attending physician recommends any restrictions or accommodations, management will work with the returning employee to determine if a reasonable accommodation is feasible. Accommodations may include alternative job assignments, and some alternative job assignments may have a different pay structure. All related details will be discussed with an employee prior to his/her return.

Active communication between employees and management while the employee is on a medical leave of absence is strongly encouraged. This communication will help facilitate an employee’s return to work, and it should include medically-based expectations for when the employee will be able to return.

Bereavement Leave

In the event of the death of your current spouse, partner in a civil union, child (including adoptive, foster, step, and in-law children), parent (including parents in-law and legal guardian), sibling, grandparent, or grandchild, you may take up to three consecutive scheduled workdays off with pay. Bereavement Leave and its length are at management’s discretion. Granted bereavement leave will be paid at the employee’s PTO rate as outlined in the employee’s pay agreement. Your supervisor may approve additional unpaid time off. Friendly Fence & Roofing Will Offer Up to two (2) Days of Bereavement pay, Proper documentation must be submitted in order to Receive PTO Rate for the date requested for bereavement.

Jury Duty or Witness Leave

Friendly Fence & Roofing supports its employees in their civic duties, including serving as jurors or as subpoenaed witnesses. If an employee receives a notice of summons to serve as a juror, he/she should notify his/her supervisor of his/her need for time off. Employees may be asked to provide the summons as proof of the need for jury duty leave. This may take the form of requiring an employee to provide written verification from the court clerk after serving.

If jury or witness service does not take the entire workday, the employee is expected to call his/her supervisor to see if he/she should report to work for the remainder of the shift.

If an employee receives a summons to serve as a witness in a legal proceeding, he/she should follow the procedures outlined above for jury duty. Witness Leave may not be granted if you volunteer to be a witness.

Jury duty and witness leave is an unpaid leave. An employee may choose to use any accrued but unused PTO while serving on jury duty. An employee may keep any monies paid by the court for jury or witness service.

Voting Leave

Friendly Fence & Roofing encourages all employees to vote in public elections. Although employees should attempt to participate in elections outside working hours, an employee may speak with management regarding unpaid leave to vote during the workday if the polls will not be open outside of the employee’s scheduled shift.

Military Leave

In accordance with state and federal laws, Friendly Fence & Roofing guarantees reemployment and other rights to any employee returning from active military service, assuming that he/she complies with all notification requirements. Notification requirements are dependent upon the duration of military service. Please see management regarding further details.

An employee’s military service may impact various employee benefits in various ways. Please speak with management regarding all details regarding how benefits will be impacted in a specific situation.

Emergency Responders’ Leave

Employees who are volunteer firefighters, reserve peace officers, or other emergency services providers will receive unpaid leave when responding to an emergency in accordance with their volunteer role. Employees should provide Friendly Fence & Roofing with as much advance notice as possible, given the specific circumstances of the situation. Friendly Fence & Roofing may, at its discretion, require documentation proving eligibility upon an employee’s completion of Volunteer Emergency Responders’ Leave. Volunteer Emergency Responders’ Leave is an unpaid leave; however, an employee may choose to use any accrued but unused time off during this otherwise unpaid leave.

Social Security & Worker’s Compensation Insurance

Friendly Fence & Roofing will automatically deduct from each employee’s paycheck that employee’s responsibilities under the Federal Insurance Contribution Act (FICA, also known as Social Security). Employees will not be required to sign a payroll deduction form related to this requirement.

In accordance with state legal requirements, Friendly Fence & Roofing also provides workers’ compensation insurance coverage for all employees at no charge to its employees. Workers’ compensation is a “no-fault” system that provides financial assistance for medical and rehabilitation expenses and a portion of lost wages to employees who become injured at work.

If an employee sustains a job-related injury or illness, he/she must immediately notify his/her supervisor. If emergency medical assistance is required, the employee should seek assistance immediately. The employee’s supervisor will ensure that all appropriate paperwork is filled out with the employee’s assistance. Management will submit all initially required forms to the insurance company.

Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance

Friendly Fence & Roofing provides eligible full-time employees with access to medical, dental, & vision insurance. Contracts are available for multiple tiers of coverage and single, couple, or family plans. Employees may begin the enrollment process after completing 90 days of full-time employment with Friendly Fence & Roofing. Information and enrollment forms may be obtained from management.

Friendly Fence & Roofing pays a flat rate towards the cost of whichever plan an employee chooses. The employee is responsible for all additional premiums. The employee’s portion of the premiums will be deducted directly from the employee's paycheck.

In accordance with applicable laws, an employee may be eligible for a continuation of medical insurance coverage upon termination of employment.

For more information regarding medical insurance, please contact management.

Retirement Plan

Eligible employees may choose to participate in the 401(k) Qualified Retirement Plan provided by Friendly Fence & Roofing. A Qualified 401(k) Retirement Plan meets the special requirements required by law for a tax-deferred profit sharing plan. Through this plan, you and Friendly Fence & Roofing are both able to invest in a fund available for income after you retire. You are eligible to participate in the 401(k) Plan after you have completed 12 months of employment with Friendly Fence & Roofing. Friendly Fence & Roofing will provide more information regarding the 401(k) Plan in a separate document.

Tuition Assistance Program

Many training opportunities exist to expand the knowledge and skills of our employees. Friendly Fence & Roofing makes a point to monitor these opportunities, and, when management feels an opportunity exists that will enhance an employee’s ability to perform his/her job, Friendly Fence & Roofing will financially support the employee’s efforts for professional development. Friendly Fence & Roofing will inform eligible employees of training opportunities that management will support. Participation in these training opportunities is usually optional, but attendance at some of these optional trainings may be considered mandatory for promotion.

Depending on the opportunity, an employee who attends the management-approved training may be paid for their time at training. Friendly Fence & Roofing may also pay for any travel time, lodging, travel costs, meals, and class fees associated with approved training. In some instances, a per diem may be provided for meal costs. Types of expenses covered are based on approval from headquarters. Extended training opportunities are granted at significant expense to Friendly Fence & Roofing. Because of this, employees may be held financially liable for any funds distributed in association with this policy if the employee does not pass or complete the course for any reason. Also at management's discretion, employees may be held liable for all monies distributed under this policy if he/she separates from employment within the first year after the completion of the course. Although the employee will be held financially responsible for this period of time, this responsibility shall in no way constitute an employment contract or negate Friendly Fence & Roofing’ policy of at-will employment.

Headquarters- Friendly Fence & Roofing will discuss all financial responsibilities and administrative details with the employee prior to signing up training. In most cases, Friendly Fence & Roofing requires employees to sign a contract outlining financial responsibilities related to this tuition assistance program.

Please speak with management for more information regarding this benefit.

EMPLOYEE DRIVER POLICY

Overview

Employees may be required to drive for Company business on a frequent basis (driving 50% or more of scheduled time or on a regular basis), or an infrequent basis (driving less than 50% of scheduled time), as part of his/her job duties. Depending on need and the nature of the Company business, an employee may be required to drive a Company owned vehicle or may use his/her own vehicle, as determined by his/her supervisor.

Eligible Drivers

The Company shall determine whether an employee is an authorized eligible driver (“Eligible Driver”) and whether he/she shall operate a Company owned vehicle or his/her own vehicle. In order to do so, the company will run an MVR prior to employment for any employees whose job descriptions require driving.

All employees who are authorized eligible drivers must always maintain a valid driver’s license, regardless of whether they are driving a Company owned vehicle or their own vehicle. The Company maintains automobile insurance for company owned vehicles. If an employee uses his/her vehicle for Company business, he/she must carry liability and property damage insurance at levels required by applicable state law.

An employee seeking authorization as an Eligible Driver shall provide the Company with a true and correct copy of his/her valid driver’s license. An employee seeking authorization as an Eligible Driver who will be using his/her own personal vehicle shall, in addition, provide the Company with a true and correct copy of his/her automobile insurance card. The Company and its agents, including but not limited to its automobile insurer, reserve the right to review a report of the employee’s motor vehicle record/violations that has been officially created or maintained by the state in which he/she holds a driver’s license. An employee seeking authorization as an Eligible Driver, including the renewal of that authorization, shall provide the Company with written permission to obtain and review this report as needed.

Rental Vehicles

An Eligible Driver may rent a vehicle for Company business with prior managerial approval. The insurance coverage offered by a rental car company should be declined as the Company’s automobile insurance policy covers rental cars used for business purposes. A rental vehicle may only be driven by an authorized driver and use of a rental vehicle for unauthorized purposes is strictly prohibited.

Guidelines

The following general driver guidelines must be adhered to when using a Company, rental or personal vehicle for business use:

· The Eligible Driver must operate the vehicle safely, follow traffic signs and signals, take precautions to avoid situations that are likely to result in an accident and follow state and local law regarding the operation of a motor vehicle.

· Operating a vehicle for company business while under the influence of intoxicants and other drugs (which could impair driving ability) is forbidden and is enough cause for discipline, up to and including termination of employment.

· While driving, attention to the road and safety should always take precedence over conducting business over the phone. “Hands free” mode via headset or speaker should be utilized while operating a vehicle for company business. Applicable state and local laws regarding cell phone usage should always be followed.

· All drivers and passengers operating or riding in a Company or personal vehicle MUST wear seat belts.

· Any traffic fines imposed while on Company business are the responsibility of the employee.

In addition to the foregoing, the following driver guidelines shall apply to employees operating Company or rental vehicles: · A company or rental vehicle may only be driven by the authorized employee.

· Company and rental vehicles are intended for authorized business use only. The use of company vehicles for unauthorized purposes is strictly prohibited.

· Smoking in company vehicles is prohibited.

· Unauthorized non-employees and non-business passengers (i.e., family, friends, hitchhikers or strangers) are prohibited from riding in company/rental vehicles.

In addition to the general driver guidelines above, the following guidelines shall apply to employees driving their own personal vehicles:

· Liability and damage to employee-owned personal autos, as well as injury to all passengers within, is the sole responsibility of the employee and is not covered by the Companies’ auto insurance. Workers’ compensation laws are applicable to all employees and business-related passengers.

· Pre Approved mileage reimbursement may be granted to employees who use their personal vehicle for company business. The mileage rate is set pursuant to the most current IRS mileage reimbursement rate, or the rate stated within the employee handbook, as applicable. Employee Responsibilities

An Eligible Driver is responsible for the following: · Acknowledging and adhering to the Companies’ Driver policy, completing the MVR Authorization Form and submitting annually the Self-Reporting Form. Failure to adhere to this policy may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment. · Notifying management of any violations or incidents that have resulted in a permanent MVR notation on his/her driving record by completing a Self-Reporting Form. · Providing the Company a copy of his/her driver’s license at the time of renewal. · Providing to the Company a copy of his/her automobile insurance card if the employee is driving his/her own personal vehicle. · Reporting any vehicle maintenance issues observed while driving a company vehicle to his/her manager; and · Reporting all accidents or incidents while driving for Company business and providing details of an accident or incident to the insurance company as requested. Reporting of Accidents/Incidents

While conducting business in a company or personal vehicle, vehicle accidents or incidents (such as vehicle damage/theft, receipt of a ticket, etc.) may occur. The following is a guideline for reporting accidents/incidents:

Accidents/incidents involving a company/rental vehicle:

· Accidents/incidents should be reported to the police, if necessary. Employees are expected to cooperate fully with authorities in the event of an incident or accident. · Employees must contact the manager as soon as possible, but not later than twenty-four (24) hours after the incident/accident. · The employee and/or his/her manager is required to provide details of the incident/accident to the insurance adjuster or insurance agent as requested. ·

The manager must contact Human Resources for Workers’ Compensation information.

Accident while driving a personal vehicle on behalf of the company:

· Employees must contact the manager as soon as possible, but not later than twenty-four (24) hours after the accident.

· Employee is responsible for submitting any claims to his/her automobile insurance carrier. · The manager must contact Human Resources for Workers’ Compensation information.

Loss of Eligibility Status

An employee will not be authorized to become and/or remain an Eligible Driver if one or more of the following exist on his/her driving record:

· Three (3) or more at-fault accidents

· One (1) or more of the below violations:

  • Driving while intoxicated or under the influence of drugs or

narcotics

  • Reckless driving (ie. racing/speed contest)
  • Aggravated assault with motor vehicle
  • Permitting an unlicensed person to drive
  • Operating a motor vehicle during a period of suspension or

revocation

  • Any violation that results in a driver’s license suspension or

revocation

· Any combination of at-fault accidents and/or the below violations which result in a total of four (4) or more incidents:

  • Driving more than ten (10) miles per hour over posted speed limit
  • Any standard violation: traffic light, stop sign, lane crossover,

failure to signal, failure to yield, prohibited cell phone use, and other types of careless driving

  • Any other unspecified moving violation
  • Accidents of any other kind not otherwise specified herein

If any of the above scenarios exist for a company driver, the company driver’s MVR will be reviewed to ensure additional violations do not occur and to determine if the driver is eligible to drive for company business and is eligible to be insured by the company insurance policy. If the Company or its agents, including without limitation, its automobile insurance carrier, excludes an employee from becoming and/or remaining an Eligible Driver, he/she shall be prohibited from driving or operating a Company owned vehicle and using or operating his/her own personal vehicle or another vehicle for Company business. In addition, an employee not considered an Eligible Driver will not be reimbursed for mileage or a car allowance.

If the ability to drive is an essential function of the employee’s job and the employee is prohibited from driving either a company or their own personal vehicle such that he/she cannot perform the job duties of his/her position, the employee may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination.

If possible, the Company will endeavor to work with the employee to reasonably resolve any job status issues if the employee loses the eligibility to drive. A resolution may not be possible if it is not reasonable or if it creates an undue hardship on the Company.

Any driver deemed excluded by the company’s insurance carrier will only be eligible to be reinstated as a company driver if the driver has met the requirements set forth by the Company and the insurance carrier at the time of review, and the insurance carrier revokes the excluded driver status. I. RESPONSIBILITIES

PROFESSIONALISM

Maintain a professional demeanor at all times.

Adhere to a professional dress code.

Engage in appropriate conversation topics.

Uphold a positive attitude.

ATTENDANCE

Be a reliable team member.

If you need to call out, please do so via phone call—no text messages.

If the CSR Manager is unavailable, contact the office instead of reaching out to your lead.

Provide at least one hour's notice when calling out.

Submit PTO and UPTO requests at least 14 days in advance with supporting notes.

For absences of three days or more within a 14-day period, a doctor’s note is required.

Direct sick day requests to HR Manager

BREAKS AND LUNCH

Follow the designated break and lunch schedule.

Take your lunch by the fifth hour if you work more than six hours.

Always clock in and out for breaks and lunches.

No working off the clock.

COMMUNICATION

Do not download the Service Titan app on personal devices.

Avoid accessing work emails from your phone.

Use official communication platforms for all work-related matters.

Refrain from discussing work topics via personal calls, texts, or social media.

Limit personal phone use while on duty; emergency calls must be communicated to a supervisor and taken outside the call center.

Keep personal phone notifications on silent or vibrate unless it’s a company-issued device.

Back to CONTENTS

COMMUNICATION PROTOCOL

Never share an employee’s personal phone number.

When emailing, reference a job number in the subject line and include a callback number.

Always copy the respective manager when communicating with another employee or department.

Use proper channels for inter-departmental communication; never approach management from another department without your manager's approval.

Always copy the respective manager when communicating with another employee or department.

CONFIDENTIALITY

As a Customer Service Representative, you are entrusted with sensitive company and customer information. It is your responsibility to maintain confidentiality at all times.

Company Information: Never disclose the location of our office or any internal operations details. If asked, inform customers that our representatives are located at our headquarters.

Customer Information: Protect all customer data, including personal details, service history, and payment information. Do not discuss or share this information outside authorized systems or conversations.

Internal Discussions: Do not share internal communications, pricing, or procedures with individuals outside the organization.

Maintaining confidentiality protects our customers, our company, and your professional integrity.

AVAILABILITY

Log into your email at the start of your shift and remain logged in until your shift ends.

Be available for incoming calls throughout your scheduled hours.

Ensure calls are categorized correctly on your dashboard and provide additional details as necessary.

CUSTOMER INTERACTION

Limit customer hold time to a maximum of two minutes and inform them if a follow-up call is needed.

Do not direct customers to check prices online.

Avoid deleting accounts or changing addresses in Service Titan.

Always document details related to customer interactions and account inquiries.

LEAD MANAGEMENT

Process leads in chronological order, handling one lead at a time and updating lead portals according

Unhandled leads should remain unread in the inbox.

Complete Clock In & Out Checklists.

Respond to all inquiries professionally and promptly.

Avoid technical jargon when communicating with customers.

CLOSING PROCEDURES

When closing, ensure that lights are off, the building is locked, gates are secured, alarms are set, and leave in pairs.

Client Concerns Resolutions

Remember that the faster we handle client concerns the less costly they are and the more likely the client will be to resume doing business with our company. Here is a list of possible ways to resolve client concerns when there is a dispute.

Workmanship Concern

Schedule the same tech back to correct the issue / do correctly.

Schedule a different tech bank to correct the issue (if client doesn’t want the same tech)

Send a tech back with a Quality Control Manager to correct the issue (for 2nd callbacks)

Scheduling Concern

Offer to flag their account so that doesn’t occur again in the future

Price-Value Concern

Review option sheet, “That was a good choice. Why did you choose that option?”

Schedule a supervisor who to re-inspect the job and talk with the client in person

Let customers know that by the end of the conversation, this will be resolved.

Let the customer know this means even if it means refunding all the money.

Ask the customer what they think would be a fair resolution.

Attitude Concern

Send a Quality Control Manager to review and correct the situation

Schedule coaching with the tech and his supervisor to review and correct.

Customer Objections

Best Practices When Handling a Lead

Respond Quickly:

Aim to contact the lead within 30 seconds to 1 minute of receiving it. Faster response times increase the chances of engagement significantly.

Personalize Your Approach:

Use the lead’s name and refer to their specific inquiry or interest. A personalized approach builds trust and shows attentiveness.

Confirm Details:

Verify the lead’s information, such as name, contact details, and service requested, to ensure accuracy before proceeding with the conversation.

Be Prepared:

Have relevant information about your product or service ready to address any questions or concerns the lead may have.

Ask Open-Ended Questions:

Engage the lead by asking questions that allow them to share more about their needs, preferences, or concerns.

Follow a Script (If Applicable):

Use a structured call or email script as a guide, but be flexible to adapt to the lead’s responses.

Be Professional and Friendly:

Maintain a polite and approachable tone to make the lead feel comfortable and valued.

Overcome Objections:

Listen carefully to any concerns and provide thoughtful responses to address their hesitations.

Track and Follow Up:

Log the interaction in your CRM or tracking system and schedule timely follow-ups if the lead isn’t ready to convert immediately.

Qualify the Lead:

Determine whether the lead is a good fit for your product or service based on their needs and readiness to act.

Avoid Pressure:

Be persuasive but not pushy. Focus on providing value and building a relationship.

Close Effectively:

If the lead is ready, guide them through the next steps, whether that’s scheduling an appointment, providing a quote, or signing a contract.

Handle Unresponsive Leads:

If the lead doesn’t respond initially, try multiple channels (phone, email, text) and vary your timing for follow-ups.

Leverage Call Center Services (If Available):

If you’re struggling to make contact or set appointments, consider utilizing a call center to assist with lead engagement.

Analyze and Improve:

Review your approach regularly and look for patterns in successful lead conversion to refine your process.

Remember: Each lead is an opportunity. Treat them with care and focus on building trust to maximize your chances of conversion.

Set rate:

What is your call process - Follow up? Establish a cadence that keeps you at the forefront without being intrusive.

"Speed to dial" refers to the time it takes for a business or sales team to contact a potential lead after they have shown interest or have been identified as a prospect. It's a crucial metric in many industries, particularly in sales and marketing, because the faster you contact a lead, the better your chances are of engaging them effectively before they lose interest or contact a competitor. Rapid response is often associated with higher conversion rates and better customer service experiences.

Timeline/speed to dial: How quickly do you respond to a lead/The faster you respond, the higher the chances of converting a lead into a set appointment.

Channels - Use multiple communication channels where appropriate (email, phone, text, social media) to increase the likelihood of engagement.

Sales Training: Regular training for your sales team to improve their negotiation skills, objection handling, and closing techniques.

Scripts: Develop and refine scripts that salespeople can use during calls to increase consistency and effectiveness.

Promotions or Discounts: Offer time-limited promotions or discounts to encourage quicker decision-making.

Customer Feedback: Regularly collect and analyze feedback from leads and customers to identify areas for improvement.

Caller ID transparency or "caller ID display." Ensuring that your business name and number are correctly displayed on the recipient's phone, making it clear who is calling. This practice helps to reduce the likelihood of your calls being blocked or ignored, as recipients are more likely to answer calls from identifiable numbers.

Issued/Demo:

Better Targeting: Refine your targeting criteria based on past successful conversions to ensure you are reaching the most receptive audience

Increase Minimum income level filter

Ease of Scheduling: Make it as easy as possible for potential customers to schedule demos. Consider automated scheduling tools that allow leads to pick times that suit them without back-and-forth communication.

Reminders: Implement automated reminders via email or SMS to reduce no-shows for scheduled demos.

Tailored Demos: Customize demonstrations to address the specific interests and needs of each prospect. This personalization can make the demo more relevant and engaging

Training: Regularly train your sales or demo team on the key features and benefits of your products, as well as on effective presentation and persuasion skills.

Communication: Maintain an open line of communication with prospects from the time they show interest until the demo, ensuring they feel valued and informed.

Immediate Follow-Up: Follow up immediately after a demo while the experience is still fresh in the prospect’s mind. This can include a summary of the demo, additional resources, and next steps.

Feedback Collection: Gather feedback on the demo experience to identify strengths and areas for improvement.

Demo Tools: Use high-quality, reliable tools for virtual demonstrations to ensure a smooth, professional experience that impresses prospects.

Prepare for Objections: Train your team to anticipate and address common objections during the demo, which can prevent conversion drop-offs.

Special Offers: Provide exclusive offers or discounts for prospects who commit shortly after a demo, adding an incentive for quick decision-making

Angi Lead Notification

When to Use: Select this for incoming calls from Angi (formerly Angie’s List) lead notifications. Typically used to track leads originating from this platform.

Call for Employee

When to Use: When the caller is attempting to reach a specific employee. This could be personal or work-related inquiries.

Calling About Current Job

When to Use: When a customer calls for updates, questions, or concerns regarding an active job that is currently in progress or scheduled.

Customer Found Someone Else

When to Use: Use this if a customer informs you they’ve chosen another provider for their service needs.

Customer Said They Would Call Back

When to Use: When a customer indicates they are not ready to book or proceed and will contact the business at a later time.

Customer Wanted Price Over the Phone

When to Use: For calls where customers inquire about pricing or quotes without scheduling an appointment or service.

Didn't Want to Pay Dispatch Fee

When to Use: When the caller declines service due to the dispatch or service fee.

Existing Customer, Inquiry About Booked Job

When to Use: When an existing customer calls for information regarding a job they’ve already scheduled.

Google Recording

When to Use: For calls originating from Google Ads or call tracking systems. This helps identify and track these marketing leads.

Hang Up

When to Use: When a call disconnects before meaningful communication or if no conversation occurs.

Information About Our Services

When to Use: For calls where the primary reason is to learn about the services your business provides.

Install Lead

When to Use: When a customer inquires about installation services, such as HVAC systems, plumbing fixtures, or similar projects.

Out of Service Area

When to Use: For calls from customers outside your geographical service area.

Seeking Employment

When to Use: When the caller is inquiring about job opportunities or submitting an application.

Service Not Provided

When to Use: For customers requesting a service your business does not offer.

Solicitor/Marketing

When to Use: For calls from vendors, marketers, or solicitors attempting to sell services or products to your business.

Spanish Speaking Customer

When to Use: For calls requiring assistance from a Spanish-speaking representative. Ensures appropriate language support is noted.

Tenant Without Permission

When to Use: When a tenant calls without authorization from the property owner or landlord to schedule or discuss service.

Vendor

When to Use: For calls from vendors supplying goods or services to your business.

Wanted Earlier Appointment

When to Use: When a customer calls to inquire about or request an earlier appointment than their currently scheduled one.

Wrong Number

When to Use: For calls clearly intended for someone else or another business.

NETWORX:

Any questions regarding your accounts to send me an email directly. When you go through the system it generates a ticket then it goes to 2 other departments first and if there is not someone checking those regularly then I may not get the message in a timely manner.

In your Networx account, there is a report that can be run or when you look at the list of leads, when you report a lead a clock timer looking thing to let you know it was reported. ANGI: These are the items that can submit for credit:

check fraud

disconnected phone number AND bounced email address

contact information for another pro/company

fraudulent messages, calls, emails or texts

Some items that cannot submit for credit are:

homeowner changed their mind

homeowner accidentally submitted the wrong type of request

receiving the same lead twice (our system automatically catches this)

SPAM is a current plague in today's society, unfortunately ANGI is not the exception to this. However, we recognize this as an issue and have a system in place to help our contractors experiencing this. If you report to me what lead you believe to be SPAM with the reasoning, I will submit for you to get a credit - which essentially means we will remove that lead from your numbers and our system will feature you back at the top to help generate fresh, real leads.

In rating the lead, if you choose to rate it a 1 or 2 star, it will go to a department that will investigate all leads that are claimed to be SPAM. If they do find the lead is a SPAM lead, they will credit any company that received it. In addition, if another company submits a lead that is credited as SPAM, you will also be credited for that. More information below!

1. Objective

A clear process for all subcontractors of Friendly Fence & Roofing to know the necessary steps to view, approve, or dispute payments in ServiceTitan.

2. Roles scope: Subcontractors and Payroll administrator 3. Previous Steps / Dependencies

All actions related to payroll completed in Service Titan for the current pay period.

SOP Video

Key Steps

TO VIEW PAYROLL

Step   Action                                                              Deadline
1      Login to Service Titan using credentials                            Saturday of

every week 2 Locate the “Overview” menu at the top left of your screen. You will notice a banner at top where you will see “Timesheets and performance pay reports ready for review”.

TO APPROVE PAYROLL

3      Click on "View" to see the dates and amounts to be paid             Saturday of

every week 4 Review the details including invoice number, customer name, gross pay and other itemized payments for materials, labor, change orders or notes of credit for returned materials

5 If you agree with the amount being paid, click on “Approve”.

TO DISPUTE PAYROLL

6 If you don’t agree with the amount being paid, click on “Dispute” Monday by A new window will open up for details about your dispute. 5:00 p.m. EST

In this window you must enter:

Name of customer Amount expected Items missing (sheets of plywood, square counts) Who was notified during the project about this situation

IF the above information is not entered, the dispute will not be evaluated for correction.

Take a Loom video showing where the discrepancy in payment is and email it to:

Payroll Administrator

Production Manager

Considerations

  • Approve your own reports for payment. If a report doesn’t get approved or

disputed by you, Management will assume that it is approved and proceed to pay the indicated amount.

  • Disputes should be handled promptly and with clear documentation to expedite

resolution.

  • Communicate any discrepancies between work order and material if possible at

the start of the project manager to avoid payment disputes.

  • Accepted supporting documentation: Loom video explanation of the discrepancy

in service titan and a description of any previous steps taken to account for the difference. i.e. Notification to PM about change orders, excess materials, etc. ( Go to www.loom.com to record your video)

  • Disputes documentation will be received NO LATER than Monday 5:00 p.m. EST.

Tips for Efficiency

  • Regularly check for pending payments to avoid delays in processing.
  • Provide thorough and detailed explanations when disputing payments to expedite

resolution.

  • Follow the standard operating procedure guidelines and contact the designated

email for any questions or clarifications.

Resolution of Payment Disputes

  • Accounting will be notified immediately after your dispute has been submitted via

Service Titan. Don’t forget to enter an email address and a telephone number.

  • After a dispute has been received by Accounting, you will receive a response within

24 hours acknowledging receipt. Resolution time will vary as each case is different and documentation is being analyzed.

Rest assured that the accounting team is working diligently to make sure all payments are processed in a timely manner and disputes are resolved as quickly as possible, if they meet the requirements.

Standard Operating Procedure

Lead Sheet Management Monthly Open, Booked, and Declined-to-Schedule Lead Tracking

1. Purpose To ensure every incoming lead is tracked consistently, worked promptly, documented clearly, and moved to the correct monthly status tab based on the final outcome.

2. Scope This SOP applies to all CSRs and team members responsible for reviewing, contacting, updating, or auditing leads in the shared lead sheet. Each month is organized into three primary status tabs: Open Leads, Calls Booked, and Calls Declined to Schedule.

3. Lead Sheet Columns Column Required Information Date Submitted The date the lead was received or submitted.

Client Name The client or prospect name exactly as provided.

Phone/Email The available phone number and/or email address.

Notes Lead Summary

Source The lead source or provider, such as Angi, Networx, or another approved source.

4. Status Tab Definitions

Tab                     Use This Tab When                         Important Rules
Open Leads              The lead has been received, but there     Continue documented outreach until the lead

has not yet been a confirmed outcome is booked or meets the criteria for Declined to or completed contact process. Schedule. Do not leave a booked or clearly declined lead in Open.

Calls Booked            An appointment has been scheduled         Move the lead here whether the appointment

after the lead was received. is scheduled for the same day or any later date. Confirm the appointment details are entered correctly in the operating system before moving the row.

Lead Sheet Management SOP

Tab                      Use This Tab When                          Important Rules
Calls Declined to        The client clearly declined, the           Examples include explicit refusal, invalid
Schedule                 information is unusable, or another        contact information,non-serviceable lead, or

documented reason prevents a number that repeatedly rings once or twice scheduling or continued contact. and disconnects after the required three-day attempt period. ANY DUPLICATE RECEIVED PRIOR TO EXPLICIT DECLINE.

AI CONTACT

DISCLAIMER —

PLEASE CONFIRM

THIS WORDING

Until the client explicitly denies scheduling an appointment through the chat tab via Service Titan, via Phone call, via Helpwise, the client will remain in Open Leads.

5. Daily Lead-Handling Workflow 1. Open the current month’s Open Leads tab at the beginning of the shift and continue monitoring it throughout the day. 2. Review the lead details before contacting the client, including the name, contact information, source, existing notes, and any Sameday or Hatch conversation. 3. Attempt contact using the approved call and follow-up process. 4. Determine the correct status based on the client response and the rules in this SOP. 5. Move the entire lead row to the correct tab. Do not copy the row and leave a duplicate behind. 6. Verify that all fields moved correctly and that the lead appears only once within the monthly tabs.

6. Three-Day Rule for One- or Two-Ring Disconnects

  • A phone number that rings only once or twice and then disconnects must not be moved to Calls Declined

to Schedule after the first occurrence.

  • The lead must be attempted across three separate days before it may be moved for this reason.
  • Each day’s attempt must be documented in the Notes column.
  • After the third documented day, the lead may be moved to Calls Declined to Schedule if the same result

continues and no other usable contact method is available.

  • If the client answers, responds by another method, or AI has an unresolved conversation with the client,

update the status based on the actual outcome instead of automatically declining the lead.

Example Notes:

  • Day 1 — 7/22, 10:15 AM: Called; rang twice and disconnected. No voicemail available.
  • Day 2 — 7/23, 1:40 PM: Called; rang once and disconnected. Second day
  • Day 3 — 7/24, 4:05 PM: Called; same result. Third day attempted. Moved to Calls Declined to Schedule

— unusable phone connection. Lead Sheet Management SOP 7. Documentation Standards

  • Enter notes immediately after each attempt or conversation.
  • Use clear, factual language. Do not enter opinions or unnecessary personal comments.
  • State why a lead was moved to Calls Declined to Schedule.
  • For booked leads, move the entire row from Open Leads to Calls Booked.
  • Review all existing note activity before contacting the client to avoid repeated questions or conflicting

communication.

8.Quality Check Done Quality Check

  • Booked leads have been moved out of Open Leads.
  • Declined leads include a documented reason.
  • One- or two-ring disconnects were not declined before the three-day requirement was completed.
  • No duplicate rows remain across the month’s status tabs.

9. Escalation Do not guess when the correct status is unclear. Leave the lead in Open Leads, document the concern, and request guidance from the CSR lead or manager before moving it.

2|P a g e Introduction Businesses that scale and attract premium buyers do not rely on luck. They rely on systems.

A sellable company produces a steady stream of high quality opportunities from multiple sources and converts them with discipline. Google LSAs, inbound calls, web forms, referrals, repeat customers, and third party aggregators all play a role in building a diversified lead engine.

Relying on one channel creates risk. Owning many channels creates leverage.

Each lead type demands a different strategy, different language, and different timing. Owners who win understand these nuances and build playbooks their teams can execute consistently.

This manual outlines the scripts, processes, and frameworks needed to convert more leads into booked appointments and more appointments into revenue. It is designed to create repeatability, accountability, and visibility inside your organization.

When your conversion process is documented and consistently followed, you reduce dependency on individuals and increase enterprise value.

That is how you Build It to Sell It.

Expectations for Success Elite teams operate with:

  • Relentless work ethic
  • Clear problem solving thinking
  • Unwavering integrity

These standards form the foundation of scalable operations and buyer ready businesses.

5|P a g e Glossary

6|P a g e Commonly Used Terminology Square (SQ) - The entire roof is measured in squares. 1 square is equal to 100 square feet. Example = 1200 Square feet is equal to 12 Square. Ridge - The ridge of the roof is the horizontal line that is at the roof peaks. Hip - The hip starts at the ridge & slopes downwards towards the drip edge. Valley - The valley is where 2 roof slopes end at the same place. Rake (gable) Edge - Rake is where the ridge ends & it has a slope. Drip (eave) Edge - The lowest part of the roof that has no slope. Flashing – Sheet metal or other material installed on top of the joints of a roof system to prevent water damage Step Flashing - Flashing that goes up the slope against the house. Pitch - How steep the roof is. Pitch is added to the square, hip, valley, rake edge & step flashing. Sheathing - Plywood over entire roof Shingles – Can be made of different materials with the main purpose of protecting underlying sheathing from the weather. Traditionally measured in squares. Trim – Installed to protect the seam in the roof along a hip or ridge Rafters – Wood or metal slats inside your home that support the sheathing and shingles. They act like the skeleton for the roof. Used with a membrane and vapor barrier, which is typically a sheet of plastic blocking air and water from permeating through Underlayment – Water-resistant, paper-like material that is laid over plywood sheathing to seal it from damaging elements such as rain and snow. Layover/overlay - Laying 1 layer of shingles over another Re-sheath/plywood - The wood under the shingles on a roof Tear off - Removing all layers of shingles Re-roof - Remove all old material & replace with new material Partial re-roof - Only replacing a section of the roof, not the entire roof Layers - There may be multiple layers of shingles on the roof Roof Slope – The incline of the roof. It is expressed as a ration of vertical rise to horizontal run, and tells you how many inches the roof rises for every twelve inches in depth. Drainage – The feature of a roof that allows it to shed water

Roof Materials Tiles - Concrete tiles Cedar shake- Wood shingles (typically do not have plywood underneath) Wood Roofing – Can be shingles or tiles Metal Roofing - Large metal sheets. Comes in vertical panels or shingles resembling slate, tile and shake. Stone-coated steel – Interlocking panels made of clay or shingles and is resistant to damage caused by heavy rains Standing Seam Metal Roofing – Named so because the aluminum or steel roofing panels meet in raised seams that interlock to keep moisture out. Asphalt composite shingles – Made from fiberglass base topped with asphalt and mineral granules. Traditional shingles. Sometimes people will call them architectural shingles; this is just a style of asphalt shingle. Solar Tiles – Solar collectors integrated into existing shingles Slate – Waterproof and resistant to mold and fungus Rubber Slate – A type of slate that looks natural and can be cut with a knife to fit intricate roofs

7|P a g e Clay and Concrete tiles – Can withstand damage from tornadoes. Good for warm and dry climates Green Roofs – Covered with plants and can improve air quality, reduce runoff and insulate homes to reduce urban heat islands. Built-up roofing – Heavy roofing consisted of layers of asphalt, tar or adhesive topped with an aggregate and is only for flat roofs Rolled roofing – Consists of long rolls of mineral-impregnated and asphalt-impregnated material topped with mineral granules Membrane roofing – Another choice for flat or very low-pitch roofs. Membrane roofs can be: Neoprene, EPDM (ethylene propylene diene monomer), Chlorinated polyethylene and chlorosulfonated polyethylene sheets, and Polymer-modified bitumens

Roof Styles Gable – Refers to the triangle spot that is formed when the two pitched areas of the roof meet Hip – Slightly more difficult to build and usually has 4 sides. Performs better in high wind areas. Dutch – It is like a hip roof with small gables at either end. Mansard – It is a four-sided design with double slopes that has very steep lower slopes, which can be flat or curved. Flat - Completely flat, no pitch, not super common in residentials home, very common for commercial buildings Shed – Similar to a flat roof but has more pitch Butterfly – Very modern design that is aesthetically unique. It provides plenty of light and ventilation but drainage is a problem Gambrel – Also called a barn roof because it has been extensively used on bards Dormer – It is an addition to an existing roof. It is a window and a roof protruding from the existing slope of the roof. M Shaped – It is a double gable roof featuring two sloped sides that meet in the middle with corresponding slopes on each side.

8|P a g e Customer Funnel

In-Person vs. Insta-Quote Estimate We cannot provide pricing over the telephone! We offer in person, free, no obligation estimates. If a customer just wants a price and does not want to meet for an in-person estimate, we can refer them over to our web page for a ballpark figure with the free insta quote.

In Person Re-Roof

  • All decision makers can be present at the time of the estimate
  • Meets all of the qualifying criteria

Insta-Quote Re-Roof

  • General Contractors
  • Insurance Claims
  • Realtors
  • Rentals
  • People Selling or Buying a Home
  • All Decision Makers are Unable to Attend Estimate

  • Select “Who will pay for the job?” and choose the option that fits the scenario.

‘Customer is different from the Tenant’ means the paying customer or “Bill To” does not live at the service location. For example, a landlord is your customer who is repairing the roof on one of their properties they rent to another family.

campaign (i.e. Self Generated Lead).

15 | P a g e One Party Objection Handling Customer: “It will just be me. She/he doesn’t need to be here. Is this one of those things where we both have to be here?” Marketer: No problem! Let me ask you, what makes you say that // That’s a great question, what makes you ask? Customer: She/he doesn’t want any part of it. She/he doesn’t want to be involved.

IF SO PROCEED TO “A”

Customer: We had another company over and they made us both be there, and we don’t want to go through that again!

IF SO PROCEED TO “B”

Customer: We just are very busy and it’s hard to get us both home together.

IF SO PROCEED TO “C”

****Anytime the customer is extremely belligerent, we can resort to “Last Straw” But the best practice is to go through our process here first.****

A. Marketer: I understand, has anyone ever explained to you why we strongly recommend both parties are there? Customer: No Marketer: Alright, well allow me to share this with you: When it comes to roofing today in 2026, there are so many options, colors, styles, not to mention installation methods. What we have found in ____ years of doing business, is that initially it sounds like a roof is pretty basic, but most people don’t sit around and think about roofing every day, (unless you work here ) so often times there are far more questions from both parties then anticipated initially. With that being said, in order to leave you with the most accurate quote, 9 times out of 10 we end up needing both party’s input. I’m sure you can appreciate that! (wait for acknowledgement/response) IF the answer is YES/I UNDERSTAND: Go to scheduling. Marketer: The good news is, we are very flexible and have opened up our schedule to accommodate all of our homeowner’s busy schedules…is it usually better to catch both of you home during the day or more towards the evening? I am actually going to have a representative in your area on ________, we could stop by at ______ or ______, which works best for both of you? IF the answer is NO, proceed to D.

B. Marketer: Wow! Let me be the first to apologize on behalf of our industry as a whole! Tell me, did they overstay their welcome too? Customer: Yes and wouldn’t leave! Marketer: That’s unfortunately not the first time I have heard that. It’s a sad part of what we do, that some companies have some procedures that just don’t put the customer first. With us, we are just a smaller locally-owned mom and pop’s type of business here so we aren’t talking suits and ties and slick talking “salesmen”. We actually have what we refer to as _______. Has anyone ever explained to you why it is that WE suggest having both people present? When the answer is NO, proceed back to A.

LAST STRAW: Whenever possible, we try to help our potential customers not spend more of their valuable time than necessary since most people today don’t have a lot of extra time to spend with an estimator more than once.
