Introduction Your reputation is built on what happens after the job is sold. From the moment materials hit the driveway to the final cleanup, the production process defines how customers perceive your brand and how efficiently you turn revenue into profit.

Delivering consistent, high-quality work on every job site is not just about the technical work. It is about communication, organization, and accountability.

The production team manages the full lifecycle of each project: scheduling, material coordination, crew oversight, quality control, and customer communication. Every Project Manager plays a key role in ensuring jobs start on time, run smoothly, and close out cleanly.

This manual outlines the processes, checklists, and standards that make that possible. You will find detailed workflows for job prep, on-site management, punch lists, customer updates, and warranty procedures designed to protect margins, minimize rework, and deliver a best-in-class customer experience.

Expectations for Success The best Project Managers combine discipline, leadership, and pride in their work. These traits separate teams that simply complete jobs from those that build lasting customer trust and company growth.

  • Discipline means being proactive, not reactive. Great teams do not wait for problems. They anticipate

them by checking forecasts, confirming materials, and walking jobs before crews arrive.

  • Leadership means owning the site. Customers, crews, and teammates look to you for direction. Set

the tone with professionalism, communicate clearly, and resolve issues quickly and decisively.

  • Pride in workmanship means never cutting corners. Every project you deliver represents your brand.

Leave every site cleaner than you found it, every customer informed, and every detail complete.

At the end of each project, the standard is simple: the job was done right, the customer is happy, and everyone involved would gladly work with you again.

7 Step Production Process Overview

Step   Function                 Responsible Party    Objective
1      Job Review and           Operations Manager   Ensure paperwork, measurements, selections, and

Approval profitability are complete so production has everything required to execute the job.

2      Assign Project Manager   Operations Manager   Match the job to the PM with the right skillset and

near-term availability.

3      Pre-Job Meeting and      Project Manager      PM introduces self to customer, confirms requirements,

Scheduling provides a clear process overview, schedules job, and handles permitting (if applicable).

4      Crew Scheduling          Project Manager      Select crew with required skillset for the scope (including

specialty work when needed).

5      Material Ordering        Project Manager      Ensure proper materials are ordered, costs align with

estimate, and delivery timing and location are confirmed.

6      Production               Project Manager      Deliver best-in-class workmanship and customer

experience from start to finish while enforcing safety standards.

7      Post-Job Closeout        Project Manager      Meet with customer to confirm expectations are met,

document follow-up, collect balance, and request a 5-star review.

Step 1: Job Review and Approval

Ensure every job entering production is fully prepared, properly documented, and operationally feasible before scheduling or material ordering begins. The goal is to eliminate preventable delays, cost overruns, and scope errors.

Operations Manager (in collaboration with Estimator/Sales and the assigned Project Manager).

Validate that all pre-production requirements have been met and documented so the production team has complete, accurate, and approved job information.

  • Collect and review job documentation. Confirm signed contracts/proposals, deposit and/or financing

approval, and job photos are uploaded. Ensure customer information, scope of work, and payment terms are accurate and complete.

  • Verify measurements and reports. Cross-check measurement outputs (e.g., Roofr, Hover, EagleView,

manual takeoffs) against the sold estimate. Confirm dimensions, accessories, and critical job factors align with the final quote. Flag inconsistencies for review.

  • Confirm selections. Validate all customer selections (materials, finishes, equipment, colors, model

numbers, and any options) are confirmed in writing and entered correctly in the system.

  • Confirm permits and special conditions. Ensure permitting requirements are known and initiated.

Identify HOA requirements, special access needs, structural considerations, utility shutoffs, or any jobsite constraints.

  • Margin and cost check. Review estimated material and labor costs to confirm job profitability meets

your target direct margin of [TARGET]%. Document any exceptions with reasoning and approval.

  • Finalize pre-production checklist. Complete the Job Readiness Checklist. Mark job as Approved for

Production and notify scheduling and PM in your FSM/CRM platform.

  • Documentation complete in CRM
  • Customer selections verified
  • Takeoff accuracy confirmed
  • Job margin meets standard
  • Ready for PM assignment and crew scheduling

Step 2: Assign Project Manager

Assign each project to the best-fit Project Manager (PM) based on expertise, current workload, and capacity. Proper PM assignment ensures quality execution and consistent customer communication throughout production.

Operations Manager

Align job type, scope, and customer needs with the PM best equipped to handle them efficiently and professionally.

  • Review upcoming approved jobs in your FSM/CRM platform. Review details including project type,

specialty work, and estimated duration.

  • Evaluate PM workloads. Assess each PM’s current active job count and projected completions over the

next 1 to 2 weeks. Consider travel distance and job complexity when balancing workload.

  • Match job complexity to PM skillset. Assign specialized projects (e.g., commercial, multi-day installs,

complex permitting, insurance-driven work, specialty systems) to PMs with relevant experience. Identify training opportunities for junior PMs when appropriate.

  • Assign PM and communicate. Assign PM within the FSM/CRM platform and include notes on customer

expectations, known site conditions, and unique constraints.

  • Conduct internal handoff. Schedule a 10 to 15 minute handoff between Operations and the assigned

PM. Review contract, site photos, notes, and material lists so the PM is fully briefed before customer contact.

  • PM confirmation. PM reviews documentation, confirms understanding, and marks acceptance in the

internal tracker.

  • PM assignment logged in FSM/CRM
  • Handoff completed
  • PM understands scope and timeline
  • Customer scheduling next steps initiated

Step 3: Pre-Job Meeting and Scheduling

Establish clear communication, expectations, and alignment between the Project Manager, customer, and production team before job start. This step ensures all technical, logistical, and customer-facing details are finalized prior to mobilization.

Project Manager

Confirm the job is fully ready for production with materials, schedule, and customer expectations aligned to prevent miscommunication, avoid rework, and ensure a smooth kickoff.

  • Contact the customer promptly after assignment using the approved pre-job call script (Exhibit A).
  • Introduce yourself as the Project Manager and set expectations for the pre-job inspection meeting.
  • Review all job documentation (measurements, photos, scope, and financing) in your FSM/CRM

platform.

  • Conduct the on-site pre-job inspection to verify site conditions, finalize measurements, confirm

selections, and identify potential risks or add-on opportunities.

  • Complete and upload the pre-job customer notice (Exhibit B) and scope of work form (Exhibit C).
  • Customer meeting completed and documented
  • Scope and materials verified
  • Permitting and scheduling confirmed
  • Pre-job forms uploaded
  • Customer expectations aligned

Exhibit A: Pre-Job Scheduling Script

If they answer

  • Hello, this is (Name) with Friendly Fence & Roofing. (Pause for comprehension)
  • I’m giving you a call regarding your upcoming project that (Salesperson Name) estimated for you.

(Pause for comprehension)

  • Great. First, I wanted to introduce myself. I will be your Project Manager, responsible for the job and

crew, and your main point of contact moving forward. (Pause for comprehension)

  • I also wanted to discuss timelines with you related to the project. (Pause for customer response)
  • Customers will either share preferred dates, upcoming trips where they do not want work happening, or

they may be fully open. Either way, respond to show you are listening. The goal from here is to schedule the pre-job Project Manager meeting.

After responding to their timing preferences, you can say:

  • Usually the first thing I like to do is schedule a time to meet with you before the job starts. The goal of

this meeting is to review the information I received, finalize my material list, get my own eyes on the job site, and confirm I have a strong plan to ensure your project runs smoothly. (Pause for customer response)

  • Typically this is about a 60-minute inspection, starting with the primary work area and any relevant

interior access (attic, mechanical room, basement, panel access, etc.), similar to what was done during the estimate.

  • Then we will do a quick sit down to share the plan and answer questions. That can take 30 to 60

minutes depending on what you may have for me. Total time on site is usually around two hours.

Offer the customer several options

  • Offer 2 to 3 time options, or confirm the time chosen based on your schedule.
  • Confirm date and time verbally and in writing (text/email).

Customer says yes Great, thank you very much. We will see you on (repeat the date and time). Have a great day.

Customer says no Offer later dates you have available. Repeat until scheduled.

If they don’t answer Voicemail: My name is (Your Name) with Friendly Fence & Roofing. I will be your Project Manager and I am reaching out to schedule your upcoming project. In order to lock in your date on our schedule, please call us back as soon as possible or respond to the email and text I am going to send you.

Do not leave dates over voicemail.

Process Description

  • Review the job
  • Verify down payment and/or financing approval
  • Review photos/videos from the sales appointment
  • Verify measurements and key job factors using available tools (photos, satellite maps, measurement

reports)

  • Initial material list generation (identify specialty conditions and accessories as applicable)
  • Identify potential errors and opportunities for added value
  • Probe subcontractors for availability before the pre-job meeting
  • Schedule pre-job meeting
  • As soon as the job is assigned, use the script above to schedule the meeting with the customer.
  • Pre-job meeting
  • Meet customer and build rapport (5 to 10 minutes)
  • Jobsite inspection and photo documentation
  • Interior inspection (where applicable) and photo documentation
  • Finalize job plan and required materials
  • Sit down meeting with customer (1 to 2 hours) to go over plan and expectations
  • Identify errors and opportunities for added value during sit down
  • Estimate any additional work needed (if discovered)
  • Set expectations for project timeframes
  • Confirm install and job walk dates/times for all scopes
  • Tentatively schedule install dates with customer
  • Set expectation that you strive for a 5-star experience and will ask for a 5-star review if delivered
  • Conclude meeting

Exhibit B: Pre-Job Customer Notice

Customer ________________________________ Proposal #__________________

Project Pre-Job Notice Thank you for contracting with us. So that your project may be as convenient and stress-free as possible, please review the items below before work begins. 1. Protect or cover all non-moveable items, especially in attics, garages, patios, basements, and storage areas. Unless specifically noted, cleanup of these areas is not included in the bid price. If you would like us to do this, we can quote a price. 2. In some projects, fasteners or nails may penetrate through decking or framing. Move any items stored tight against decking, sheathing, or mechanical chases. 3. Truck and equipment access to the work area is critical. Trim back low hanging tree limbs and/or overgrown landscaping that may impede access. Move cars, boats, RVs, etc. from driveways and nearby work zones to prevent damage from falling debris and to ensure access. 4. If you have treasured items that cannot be moved, please notify your foreman or Project Manager before work begins. 5. Our crew may require access to electricity for tools and equipment. Breakers can trip, and in rare situations, improper electrical conditions may be discovered when running high amperage tools. 6. Remove glass shades from hanging lamps and remove pictures from walls and fragile items from shelves. We are not responsible for interior damage caused by vibrations from construction work. 7. Cover areas under skylights, ceiling penetrations, or attic access points to protect the interior from dust or debris. 8. Notify us of any vaulted or wood ceilings, and any electrical, plumbing, HVAC, or low-voltage components in areas where fasteners may be used, to prevent damage from penetration. 9. Depending on the project, dust may be present. Cleaning dusty items is not included in the bid price. 10. Painting of replaced wood or trim is not included unless specifically addressed in the contract. 11. Even with careful handling, moldings, trim, skylights, gutters, antennas, alarms, cable, satellite dishes, condensate lines, and exterior fixtures may come loose, break, or be damaged during construction. There may be an additional charge to replace or repair these items. 12. We are not responsible for pest control. Any pest-related problems require a separate extermination contractor. 13. We cannot be responsible for driveway cracks that exist or may develop due to construction vehicles. We plan to use the driveway for loading and unloading materials and debris. Avoiding driveway use may result in an extra charge. 14. Repair of cracks or nail pops that may develop in drywall, lath, or plaster from construction vibrations is not included in the bid price. 15. As with all construction, noise is a factor. If this is an inconvenience, it is advisable to make other arrangements during installation. 16. Light may reflect in attics or interior cavities around walls, chimneys, penetrations, and mechanical chases. This is normal and does not indicate a leak or flaw. 17. Determining the presence of or working with mold, asbestos, lead paint, or other hazardous materials will result in additional work being performed by separate contractors. 18. On projects with exposed soffits or thin coverings, fasteners may protrude and paint may chip. Repair is not included unless stated in the contract.

19. Unless noted in the contract, certain behind-the-wall or concealed components are not replaced as part of the project (for example, roof-to-wall flashing, hidden plumbing, concealed wiring, or buried lines). 20. We are not responsible for any color or finish choices beyond ordering and installing the specified selections on the contract. 21. EXTRA MATERIALS: We order extra materials for every job and return them to the supplier for credit on a regular basis. Extra materials left over on the jobsite are not included in the bid and no credits will be issued. 22. Structural settling can occur over time. Repairs to sagging framing or structural members are not included unless specifically addressed. Completing the project alone will not necessarily change existing lines or levels. 23. If existing guttering or drainage is not removed and replaced, we are not responsible for ensuring it is sloped correctly. Replacing one gutter profile with another can result in exposed fascia or paint. Painting is not included unless stated. 24. During peak season, materials may be delivered several working days in advance depending on supplier availability. 25. We work in most weather conditions and crews are trained to work in light precipitation when safe. Jobs may be moved if the foreman does not feel comfortable starting due to forecast and safety conditions. 26. Typical payment terms are: [Populate your standard terms]. Special terms may be arranged for larger projects. 27. If the project is delayed due to homeowner request, there may be additional charges due to material cost increases.

Step 4: Crew Scheduling

Ensure every project is paired with the correct subcontractor or crew based on technical skillset, reliability, and schedule availability. Proper crew assignment protects quality, efficiency, and on-time project delivery.

Project Manager

Coordinate the right crew, at the right time, with the right materials and information to deliver a flawless installation experience.

  • Review job scope and skill requirements. Determine if specialty crews are required (for example: steep

work, complex mechanical installs, panel upgrades, trenching, guttering, insulation). Reference your subcontractor roster and prior performance.

  • Check crew availability. Review master scheduling/dispatch board and contact preferred crews to

confirm available dates and workload capacity.

  • Assign crew. Match crews based on experience, reliability, and historical performance (quality,

callbacks, completion time). Assign a backup crew when needed.

  • Send work order. Email or send a work order including scope, jobsite address, photos, expected start

date/time, safety requirements, and special notes. Attach job plan and photo links.

  • Crew confirmation and CRM update. Require written acknowledgement confirming start date and

scope acceptance. Update the FSM/CRM platform.

  • Daily schedule tracking. Maintain visibility in the schedule to ensure on-time starts and address gaps or

cancellations immediately.

  • Crew audit. Twice annually, audit required documentation (insurance, safety documents, agreements,

licenses). For infrequently used specialty crews, audit before scheduling.

  • Crew confirmed and acknowledged
  • PM and Operations notified
  • Backup crew available for contingencies

Step 5: Material Ordering

Ensure all materials are accurately selected, ordered, and scheduled for delivery to align with the project timeline and budget. Proper material management eliminates delays, reduces waste, and protects target margins.

Project Manager (with oversight from Operations and coordination with supplier partners)

Confirm that all materials, finishes, quantities, and delivery logistics are correct and aligned with the approved job scope before installation begins.

  • Follow your FSM/CRM material workflow (Exhibit D) to add materials, verify quantities, and finalize

selections per the estimate.

  • Double-check measurement data and site conditions to validate quantities and ensure selection

consistency across components.

  • Confirm purchase orders are created, coded to the job (use job number as PO number), and routed to

the correct supplier.

  • Schedule delivery to arrive prior to crew start. Ensure dumpster, portable restroom, protection

materials, and any special equipment timing aligns with schedule.

  • Material quantities verified against measurement report
  • Selections confirmed
  • PO routed to correct vendor
  • Delivery timing aligned with crew schedule
  • Receipts uploaded to CRM

Exhibit D: Material Ordering Workflow (Example:

ServiceTitan) Use this as an example workflow. Adapt labels to your FSM/CRM configuration.

Step Action 1 Once in ServiceTitan, navigate to "Follow Ups".

2 Click on your selected "Sold Estimate".

3 Click on "Estimate Job Number" (blue link).

4 Scroll to Notes, read, and copy all relevant information into the "Job Summary" screen of the new installation job.

5 Click the "Files" tab to find the measurement report (e.g., Roofr, Hover).

6 Open the report file (often labeled like "JOB ADDRESS.pdf").

7 Return to the sold estimate to continue the job booking process.

9 Click "Edit Variation".

11 Click "Save" for each item. Complete all items at this time.

12 Click "Save" and "Add". Keep the measurement report open on a second screen for quantity input.

13 Click the quantity field and input quantities needed for each item.

14 Continue until all material lines are complete. When ready to order, click "Initiate Requisition".

23 Click "Transactions".

25 Next to Actions, click "Select as PDF" (or equivalent).

Step 6: Production

Oversee all on-site work to ensure each project is executed safely, efficiently, and to company quality standards. The production phase represents the company’s brand promise in action and directly determines customer satisfaction and profitability.

Project Manager (with Operations support)

Deliver a best-in-class customer and jobsite experience, on time, on budget, and defect-free, while maintaining safety compliance and accurate documentation.

  • Confirm materials and crew arrival per schedule.
  • Conduct a pre-start walkthrough with the customer to reconfirm expectations, review site protection

measures, and display required signage.

  • Supervise daily operations, enforce safety standards, and ensure work aligns with approved plans.
  • Document progress with before/during/after photos in your CRM.
  • Proactively communicate with the customer and address concerns promptly.
  • Conduct interim quality checks and verify materials and installations meet specification.
  • At completion, ensure full cleanup, final inspection, and customer satisfaction before leaving the site.

Job Start Checklist

  • Portable restroom or jobsite facilities (if applicable)
  • Signage and safety barriers (as required)
  • Yard signs or jobsite branding (if used)
  • Safety paperwork signed and uploaded (fall protection, lockout/tagout, trenching, etc. as applicable)
  • Material list paperwork printed or available on site
  • Permit posted on site (if applicable)
  • Critical consumables on hand (for example: protective coverings, sealants, underlayment, fittings)

Purchase Order Creation (FSM/CRM)

  • If additional material is needed, a purchase order must be generated in your FSM/CRM platform.
  • Open the job invoice, click Actions, and select Add PO.
  • Select vendor and PO type, choose pickup or delivery method.
  • In the summary field, type a brief description explaining why you need the material.
  • In the vendor invoice field, add the supplier receipt reference when available (or order number for retail

purchases).

  • Add equipment and materials, confirm quantities, then save.
  • Obtain a copy of the receipt and upload to the job record in CRM.

Material Pickup and Delivery

  • Coordinate pickup from approved supplier or distributor if needed.
  • Subcontractors should not use personal funds to buy supplies. Use approved purchasing methods

(phone sale, PO, or company card per policy).

  • Oversee delivery to job site and verify all items are accounted for and in good condition.
  • Report shortages immediately so they do not impact schedule.

Troubleshooting Customer Concerns

  • Be readily available to address questions or concerns during the project.
  • Provide proactive updates on progress, including unexpected delays or challenges.
  • Work collaboratively to find solutions and document agreements in writing.

Quality Assurance

  • Conduct frequent inspections throughout the project to ensure work is performed according to industry

standards and project specifications.

  • Verify the quality and condition of materials used in the installation.

Cleanup and Site Restoration

  • Ensure the jobsite is kept clean and free of debris throughout the project.
  • Restore the customer’s property to its original condition, including landscaping and any damaged areas

within scope.

Payment Collection and Documentation

  • Invoices are provided by the office or generated per your finance process.
  • Collect payment per agreed terms and obtain required signatures for completion and payment receipt.

Project Reporting

  • Provide regular updates on project progress to internal team (group chat, job notes), including

challenges, solutions, payments, and completed tasks.

  • Record key dates, customer interactions, and significant issues in CRM.
  • Share photos before, during, and after completion for visual documentation.

Step 7: Post-Job Closeout

Ensure every project concludes cleanly with full customer satisfaction, completed documentation, and final payment collected. Closeout protects profitability and brand reputation.

Project Manager

Confirm workmanship meets company standards, customer is fully satisfied, and all financial, material, and administrative steps are complete to close the project in the system.

Detailed Process

  • Schedule and conduct the post-job walk with the customer.
  • Complete the 25-point inspection, confirm all punch items are addressed, and collect the final payment.
  • Capture before-and-after photos and ensure the customer receives copies of warranties and

documentation.

  • Upload material returns, supplier receipts, and subcontractor invoices into CRM.
  • Record customer feedback, obtain a 5-star review, and confirm any warranty registration.
  • Verify all files are complete and update project status to Closed.

Overview: Post-Job Walk The post-job walk is typically the final jobsite and customer visit associated with your project. The purpose is to verify the installation, ensure the customer is satisfied, and collect final payment before issuing warranties or final documentation.

The meeting can be broken down into the following steps:

  • 25-point inspection
  • Final site cleanup (if needed)
  • Photo sharing with customer
  • Collect final payment
  • Request 5-star review
  • Send warranty and documentation
  • Close job in FSM/CRM same day

Site Clean Up

  • Magnet sweep for nails/fasteners (repeat even if crew has done it). If the site has excessive fasteners,

notify foreman for accountability.

  • Ensure excess materials are removed and returned to supplier.
  • Ensure portable restroom/trailer is removed (if applicable).
  • Leave the site better than you found it. Often sweeping leaves or tidying adjacent areas is a simple

touch that earns a 5-star review.

Payment

  • If financed: Submit request for payment through the lender portal. Confirm customer has completed

any required approval steps before leaving.

  • If not financed: Collect check or process payment for final balance. Confirm deposits already paid with

office and verify remaining balance due.

5-Star Review

  • Confirm the customer feels they received a 5-star experience.
  • Ask for the review and make it easy. Send the link or use a QR code/review card.

Warranty and Closeout

  • Ensure customer is clear on warranty next steps.
  • Complete material returns and upload receipts (Exhibit F).
  • Leave final notes and mark job Complete/Closed the same day.

Appendix A: Customer Communication Overview

Every customer contact is an expensive, precious resource. We exist solely because customers choose to do business with us over competitors. If we forget this, we lose. We are a customer business, not a trades business.

To ensure customers feel this, we must be:

  • Attentive: Listen to concerns, write them down, and repeat back to confirm understanding.
  • Responsive: Return calls/emails quickly (8 business hours or less). Never blow them off or forget to

call.

  • Understanding: Clarify that you understand the problem. Restate it back: “Just to be sure I’m

understanding you, what you are saying is…?” Seek to understand first, then seek to be understood.

  • Listen: Two ears, one mouth. Never cut off a customer. Never dismiss anything they say. Write down

all concerns.

  • Empathetic: Their problem is our problem. Show that you care and feel their pain.
  • Respectful: Respect people’s time. You are on their clock. Respect complaints whether founded or

unfounded.

  • Don’t try to win: If we try to win, we already lost. Nobody has ever won an argument with a customer.

Do not

  • Dismiss anything they say. If they say it, it is important to them.
  • Shift blame to coworkers. Present a unified front. Use phrasing like: “That’s unusual. I’m going to look

into that and get it resolved.”

  • Blame the customer. This is the kiss of death. Customers generate future business through referrals

and reviews.

Damage control

  • Accept responsibility and reassure them that you care.
  • Let them know you will expedite a solution and when they can expect to hear back.
  • Get the facts. Extract specifics, not vague statements (e.g., “what exactly is wrong?”).
  • Seek to understand why it is important to them if it is not obvious.
  • Get the information to the right people.
  • Do not dramatize the issue. Stick to the facts.
  • Follow up even if it is just to say you are working on it.

Professional Communication We believe in “Constant Contact”. Customers should feel like they are our only customer. They should never feel like they cannot get a response from their Project Manager. Impromptu calls are encouraged to update or simply check in throughout the project.

Words and Phrases to Avoid Words / Phrases to Avoid Alternatives Pricing / Cost / Charge Amount or Investment

Cancel Avoid the word; use “reschedule” or “adjust”

My guys Installers / Technicians / Crew

Decision maker Owner / Primary contact

I don’t understand what you’re saying Could you please repeat that?

That isn’t right Let me double check that.

Wife / Husband Spouse / Partner

Um, uh, etc. Pause silently if needed

You’re wrong Let me look into this a bit more and get back to you.

Cheap Less expensive

Guys / Gals They / Team

That doesn’t make sense Help me understand…

Swearing Don’t do it

10-Step Resolution Process 1. Let the customer vent

  • Listen
  • Don’t interrupt
  • Have empathy
  • Explain why the situation exists (when appropriate)

2. Restate the customer’s position

  • Make sure you understand
  • Check for other issues
  • Get all issues on the table before moving forward
  • Ask: “Is there anything else?”

3. Establish positive ground

  • Ask about positive aspects of the project
  • Bring up positives
  • Put the issue into perspective
  • Customer needs to understand you are acting ethically

4. Explain how the issue came to be

  • Usually there is a logical reason your customer does not know
  • Help them understand

5. Expect a rebuttal

  • This is normal. Don’t make it personal
  • Expect them to say they won’t accept it
  • Let them vent
  • Be patient. Don’t argue

6. State the relationship goal

  • Your goal is to make sure they are satisfied
  • Appeal to fair play
  • Ask: “What is fair and right?”

7. Expect a rebuttal (again)

  • Be patient
  • They may continue to complain
  • Be prepared for emotional dialogue

8. The crystal ball

  • Ask them to pretend: If we had known in advance we would run into this issue, what would we have

done differently?

  • Respond: “See, we are not taking advantage of you.”

9. Expect a rebuttal (budget constraints)

  • They may say they are tapped out on cash
  • Be firm, not tough
  • Revisit what is fair and right
  • Find out what would make them happy
  • Be patient

10. Confirm in writing

  • Resolution must be in writing between company and customer
  • Remain patient

Escalation to Upper Management (If Necessary) Escalation should be a last resort after multiple phone calls and in-person meetings have been executed with the intent of resolving the issue. Leadership should be informed during conflicts and is available for advice. However, passing a customer directly to upper management is a last resort after no resolution has been reached through multiple scheduled resolution attempts.

Project Managers may offer a reduction to the final balance only after all available alternatives have been exhausted (repairing, fixing, discussing, etc.). To expedite resolution, PMs may offer up to 10% off the balance without approval up to a maximum of $5,000. Amounts above this must be approved by Operations. Typically this reduction is held against the PM’s margin pay, dollar for dollar.

Appendix B: Profit Margins and Job Allowances

The targeted direct profit margin for every job is 30-40%.

Direct margin is the income percentage generated when all direct costs associated with the job are subtracted from revenue. Direct costs include direct materials, direct labor, consumable production supplies, and sales commissions.

Project Managers are responsible for protecting margin to the best of their ability and should capture change orders when unforeseen expenses arise.

If estimation errors occur, you may choose not to change order those errors to keep alignment with a “no surprises” promise. When such errors arise, the Project Manager must document in detail the costs associated with the error and how it affects margin.

You should head into your pre-job meeting with a plan for which subcontractor or crew you want to use and an idea of availability. Reach out to 1 to 3 crews so you have options.

every week 4 Review the details including invoice number, customer name, gross pay and other itemized payments for materials, labor, change orders or notes of credit for returned materials

Considerations

  • Approve your own reports for payment. If a report doesn’t get approved or

disputed by you, Management will assume that it is approved and proceed to pay the indicated amount.

  • Disputes should be handled promptly and with clear documentation to expedite

resolution.

  • Communicate any discrepancies between work order and material if possible at

the start of the project manager to avoid payment disputes.

  • Accepted supporting documentation: Loom video explanation of the discrepancy

in service titan and a description of any previous steps taken to account for the difference. i.e. Notification to PM about change orders, excess materials, etc. ( Go to www.loom.com to record your video)

  • Disputes documentation will be received NO LATER than Monday 5:00 p.m. EST.

Tips for Efficiency

  • Regularly check for pending payments to avoid delays in processing.
  • Provide thorough and detailed explanations when disputing payments to expedite

resolution.

  • Follow the standard operating procedure guidelines and contact the designated

email for any questions or clarifications.

Resolution of Payment Disputes

  • Accounting will be notified immediately after your dispute has been submitted via

Service Titan. Don’t forget to enter an email address and a telephone number.

  • After a dispute has been received by Accounting, you will receive a response within

24 hours acknowledging receipt. Resolution time will vary as each case is different and documentation is being analyzed.

Rest assured that the accounting team is working diligently to make sure all payments are processed in a timely manner and disputes are resolved as quickly as possible, if they meet the requirements.

1. Basic Business Information & Trade Specialty

  • What is your primary trade or specialty? (e.g., roofing, siding, electrical, plumbing).
  • How long has your business been in operation?
  • Are you a sole proprietor, LLC, or Corporation?
  • Can you provide references from other general contractors or clients? (Optional)

2. Licensing & Insurance (Non-Negotiable)

  • Are you licensed to work in this specific state/county?
  • Do you carry General Liability Insurance?
  • Do you carry Workers' Compensation?
  • Do you have any specialized certifications? (optional)

3. Team Capacity & Scale

  • How many people are on your permanent team?
  • Do you use your own employees or do you sub-out your work to others? (no double

subbing)

  • What is your minimum crew size?
  • Who is the designated English-speaking lead/foreman on-site at all times?

4. Availability & Reliability

  • What is your current lead time?
  • Are you available for emergency or last-minute calls?
  • Can your team work weekends if a project falls behind due to weather?
  • What is your policy for showing up on time? (How do you handle delays?).

5. Safety Protocols

  • Do you have a written safety program?
  • What PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) does your crew wear daily?
  • How do you handle fall protection on steep-slope jobs?
  • Who is responsible for daily site cleanup? "nail-sweeps" and debris removal

7. Quality Control & Warranty

  • How do you handle "call-backs" or repairs if a customer isn't satisfied?
  • What is your process for documenting "hidden damage" before proceeding with extra

work?

8. The "Field Test" Questions

  • How do you protect the homeowner’s property (landscaping, windows, AC units)

during tear-offs?

KPI Scorecard Playbook This outlines the core KPI Scorecard elements within our Standard Operating Procedures. It encompasses universal rules, CSR, Rehash/ISR, Sales, and Leadership KPIs, along with Sales Activity Standards and basic business principles.

Key Areas:

  • Universal Rules: Foundational guidelines for all team members.
  • CSR KPI Scorecard: Metrics for Customer Service Representatives.
  • Rehash KPI Scorecard: Metrics for Inside Sales Representatives.
  • Sales KPI Scorecard: Metrics for the Sales Team.
  • Leadership Review KPIs: Metrics reviewed by Leadership.
  • Sales Activity Standards: Expected sales activities and benchmarks.
  • Core business values and operational principles.

Purpose of This Playbook This document establishes clear non-negotiable performance standards across Sales, Marketing, Operations, Inventory and Leadership.

KPIs are minimum expectations not goals. Accountability removes ambiguity. Consistency drives predictable results.

How To Use This Document

  • KPIs are reviewed weekly or monthly as defined
  • Missed KPIs trigger coaching not debate
  • Barriers are logged in the Gap Log
  • Leaders own enforcement and consistency
  • Standards apply to everyone without exception

If it is not measured it cannot be coached. If it is not enforced it is not a standard.

Universal Accountability Rules

  • Minimum standards not stretch goals
  • Training ramps are defined and finite
  • Data drives conversations not emotion
  • Leaders own misses first
  • Support is documented through the Gap Log

Strong standards raise performance and filter talent naturally.

CSR KPI SCORECARD

Role Objective: Create consistent opportunity flow through disciplined call activity.

Minimum Performance Standards

                  KPI                               Standard             Review
 Inbound and outbound calls                244 calls per day         Daily
 Booking Rate                              90%+ - Inbound            Daily

30%+ - Outbound

Non Negotiable Standard Call volume is the job. Coaching begins only after 244 calls per day is met.

Rehash/ISR KPI SCORECARD

Role Objective: Recover revenue from unsold opportunities reduce lead waste and maximize marketing ROI.

Core Definitions

ISR: Inbound Sales Representative responsible for outbound follow up on unsold estimates, unbooked calls and aged leads.

Rehash Program: Structured process to re-engage no sales cancelled calls and estimates that did not close the same day.

Minimum Performance Standards

                   KPI                        Standard            Review Cadence
Saved calls rate                        15-25%                Weekly
Rebook rate from no sale follow up      10-20%                Weekly
Revenue recovered per ISR               Tracked weekly        Weekly
Average days to save                    <7 days               Weekly

If the saved call rate is 10% the script timing or ownership is broken.

Outbound Activity KPIs

                   KPI                            Standard          Review Cadence
Outbound calls per ISR per day            75-125                   Daily
Contacts made per day                     15-30                    Daily
Contact rate                                 20-30%                  Weekly
Voicemail drop usage                         100%                    Daily

Speed and volume matter more than perfection.

Follow Up Discipline KPIs

               KPI                     Standard             Review Cadence
No sale follow up attempted       100%                  Daily
Follow up attempts per lead       6-8 attempts          Weekly
First follow up timing            Within 24 hours       Daily
Multi channel follow up           Call/text/email       Weekly

If it is not attempted, it was abandoned.

Revenue KPIs

               KPI                           Standard            Review Cadence
Revenue per saved call            Tracked                       Weekly
Cost per recovered dollar         Lower than Paid CPA           Monthly
Rehash close rate                 10-20%                        Monthly
ISR influenced revenue            Tracked                       Monthly

ISR revenue should always outperform cold marketing ROI.

Pipeline Management KPIs

KPI Standard

Open rehash leads aged <30 days 100%

Unworked leads are silent profit leaks.

If a KPI does not affect

  • Profit

  • Capacity

  • Exit value

It is not a KPI.

Operations Manager – Job Description We are seeking an experienced and hands on Operations Manager to oversee day to day business operations and ensure consistency, efficiency, and accountability across the organization. This role is critical to removing the owner from daily firefighting and building systems that allow the company to scale profitably.

This is a full time position. Typical work hours are Monday through Friday, with occasional flexibility required based on operational needs.

Key Responsibilities

Operations Management: Oversee daily operations to ensure workflows run smoothly across departments. Implement, document, and enforce standard operating procedures. Identify operational gaps and lead continuous improvement initiatives. Ensure quality control and consistent execution across teams. Serve as the primary point of accountability for operational performance.

Leadership and Accountability: Lead and manage department managers and team leads. Establish clear expectations, KPIs, and accountability rhythms. Partner with leadership to execute strategic initiatives. Support team development and performance improvement.

Process and Systems: Build scalable systems that support growth and consistency. Improve communication between departments. Monitor operational metrics and adjust processes as needed.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations, or a related field preferred.
  • 5+ years of experience in operations management required.
  • Strong leadership and people management skills.
  • Experience building and enforcing SOPs.
  • Ability to problem solve and make data driven decisions.
  • Experience in home services or construction is preferred.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary and benefits package.
  • Opportunities for advancement and leadership growth.
  • A fast paced environment focused on scale and execution.

INTRODUCTION

Hello! We are excited to welcome you to Friendly Fence & Roofing.

Here at Friendly Fence & Roofing, we pride ourselves on creating a warm, team-focused atmosphere where cooperation and support are central to our operations. We hope that you will find our company to be a welcoming, engaging, and fair place to work!

This handbook presents a number of key concepts for our company. Some of these represent legal standards that we adhere to. Other aspects outline our expectations for employees and what employees can expect from us. We strongly encourage you to read this handbook in its entirety and keep it in a location where you can easily access it as a valuable resource and reference.

SECTION 1: ADMINISTRATIVE POLICIES AND PROCEDURES

Employment At-Will

Employment with Friendly Fence & Roofing is on an at-will basis. Because of this, employment may be terminated by either Friendly Fence & Roofing or the employee with or without cause, and with or without notice, at any time.

No one other than the Friendly Fence & Roofing owner/president has the authority to create an employment relationship other than on an at will basis, and he/she may only do so based upon a signed written agreement between the owner/president and the employee. Nothing contained in this or any other document provided to the employee is intended to be, nor should it be, construed as a contract that employment or any benefit will be continued for any period of time.

Furthermore, the terms and conditions of employment with Friendly Fence & Roofing may be modified at the sole discretion of Friendly Fence & Roofing with or without cause and with or without notice. Examples of the types of terms and conditions of employment that are within the sole discretion of Friendly Fence & Roofing include, but are not limited to,: promotion; demotion; transfers; hiring and discharge decisions; compensation; benefits; qualifications; discipline; layoff or recall; rules; hours and schedules; work assignments; job duties and responsibilities; reduction, cessation, or expansion of operations; sale, relocation, merger, or consolidation of operations; determinations concerning the use of equipment, methods, or facilities; or any other terms and conditions that Friendly Fence & Roofing may determine to be necessary for the safe, efficient, and economic operation of its business.

Protected Classes

Multiple policies within this handbook refer to “protected classes.” Protected classes include, but are not limited to, the following:

race,

color,

sex (including pregnancy),

religion,

age,

national origin or ancestry,

physical or mental disability,

genetic information,

veteran status, and

any other considerations made unlawful by federal, state, or local laws.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Friendly Fence & Roofing provides equal opportunities to all employees regardless of membership or perceived membership in a protected class. All such discrimination is unlawful and prohibited by Friendly Fence & Roofing. Equal employment opportunity applies to all personnel decisions and actions, including but not limited to: hiring, promotion, termination, compensation, leave of absence, and training.

Immigration Laws

Although Friendly Fence & Roofing does not unlawfully discriminate based upon citizenship status or national origin, Friendly Fence & Roofing requires that all employees be eligible to work within the United States. In compliance with the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986, Friendly Fence & Roofing requires that all employees have a completed Employment Eligibility Verification Form I-9, including providing necessary documentation establishing identity and employment eligibility.

If you have any questions regarding employment eligibility verification, please speak with management.

Reasonable Accommodation for Pregnancy and Disability

Friendly Fence & Roofing will make a reasonable accommodation for the known disability of any qualified individual who is otherwise able to perform the essential functions of his/her position. Reasonable accommodations include those that do not cause an undue hardship on the company or its employees. Any accommodation that creates an unsafe working environment for either the employee, other employees, or customers will be deemed to be unreasonable for the purposes of this policy.

Reasonable accommodations may be available to individuals with both permanent and temporary disabilities, and options may include transfers to positions with less strenuous or hazardous physical requirements.

Employees or applicants who have a disability, including pregnancy, should speak with management regarding any needed accommodations. Management will engage in an interactive process with the employee to determine whether a reasonable accommodation can be made. Management reserves the right to require medical certification of any accommodations required.

Please note: employees who are currently using illegal substances or improperly using restricted substances, such as prescription medication, are excluded from this policy.

Commitment to Diversity

At Friendly Fence & Roofing, we are committed to honoring the diverse backgrounds represented by our employees. This diversity is a source of strength, and, as such, we will strive to provide all employees the opportunity to participate and contribute to the success of Friendly Fence & Roofing. To that end, Friendly Fence & Roofing will accommodate special requests that do not constitute a threat to safety of the employee, other employees, or customers or present an undue hardship on the company or its other employees.

If an employee or applicant requires an accommodation based upon a religious belief or practice, he/she should speak with management immediately to determine whether an accommodation can be made. Similarly, if management becomes aware through other methods that a religious accommodation may be required, management may approach any impacted employee(s).

Similarly, Friendly Fence & Roofing strives to make its policies and practices fair to all employees and applicants. However, if any policy or practice of Friendly Fence & Roofing impacts an employee or applicant based upon his/her membership in a particular group or class (i.e., a “protected class”), the employee or applicant should speak with management regarding his/her concerns.

We encourage all employees and applicants to present his/her concerns in writing, as this method allows management the greatest opportunity to fully consider the area of concern. However, employees and applicants may also bring their concerns to management verbally. Management will engage in an interactive process with the impacted employee(s) to determine what, if any, reasonable accommodation may be made. If more than one reasonable accommodation exists, management reserves the right to make the final determination regarding the method or accommodation implemented.

Complaint Reporting Procedure

Although Friendly Fence & Roofing strives to make our company a professional and friendly place to work, there may be times when an employee feels that this has not occurred. In the event that an employee wishes to place a complaint, either about another employee or about a company practice, he/she is strongly encouraged to do so. Especially when that concern is regarding an incident of unlawful discrimination, sexual harassment, other harassment, retaliation, or denial of accommodation, Friendly Fence & Roofing recommends that an employee present a formal complaint to management so that the employee’s concern may be thoroughly investigated and, if found to be substantiated, addressed.

If you believe that you have been subject to or witnessed illegal discrimination, including sexual or other forms of unlawful harassment, you should complain directly to your immediate supervisor. If your immediate supervisor is directly involved, does not address your concerns, or you feel uncomfortable presenting your concerns to your immediate supervisor, you should report your concerns to any other member of management.

You are strongly encouraged to present your concerns in writing. A form for submission of a complaint can be obtained through asking your supervisor or any other member of management, and all employees are encouraged, but not required, to use this form if making a written complaint. However, if you are unable to do so, you may also lodge a complaint verbally.

If a supervisor receives a complaint from an employee, he/she is required to report the complaint to upper management for investigation. Furthermore, supervisors are required to report ALL suspected harassment, discrimination, or retaliation directly to management, even if no formal complaint has been placed by an employee. Management and supervisors will be held responsible for any discrimination, harassment, or retaliation that they commit or allow subordinates to commit. Failure to report discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or a complaint to upper management will be considered a violation of this policy.

All complaints will be thoroughly investigated by management in a manner ensuring, to the best of management’s ability, the confidentiality of all involved parties. Furthermore, all information concerning a complaint or occurrence will be kept on a “need to know” basis, and details will not be shared with uninvolved parties unless required by law.

If the investigation determines that conduct was performed against company policy or legal requirements, management will take immediate and appropriate corrective action, up to and including immediate termination of employment for any offending party.

Friendly Fence & Roofing will not tolerate or permit retaliation for filing a complaint by management, employees, or third parties.

Suggestions and Ideas

At Friendly Fence & Roofing, we encourage all employees to present any suggestions or ideas for improvement to their supervisors or management. We firmly believe that sometimes some of the best ideas come from those people who are in the field, day in and day out. As such, management will take any suggestions seriously and investigate which may be practical to implement on either an individual or company-wide basis. We encourage employees to provide a written suggestion; however, verbal discussions are also welcome at any time.

Employment Status

Employee benefits and overtime status are based upon a number of factors, including employment classifications. These classifications are presented below. A specific employee’s classification may be changed at any time with or without notice by management, so long as such change is compliant with federal and state legislation.

Exempt – employees whose job duties qualify for overtime and minimum wage regulation exemptions under federal and state law. These employees are normally expected to work full-time, and they are ineligible for overtime compensation.

Non-Exempt – employees who are compensated for any overtime worked. Please see the “Overtime” policy below for further details.

Part-Time Employees – employees who are not in a temporary status and who regularly are scheduled to work fewer than 40 hours each week. Part-time employees, may, on occasion, be required to work 40 or more hours per week; however, these requirements are considered temporary in nature. Part-time employees are generally ineligible for benefits. Any exceptions due to Federal or State law or individual agreement will be discussed related to the specific benefit.

Full-Time Employees – employees who are regularly scheduled at least 40 hours per week. Full-time employees are generally eligible for all benefits available for employees but are subject to the terms and conditions presented for each benefit.

Temporary Employees – employees who are hired to fulfill a temporary requirement for Friendly Fence & Roofing. These employees are hired for a specific duration or to fulfill a specific need. Temporary employees are not eligible for any benefits unless informed otherwise by management. Employment beyond the initially agreed upon period does not in any way imply a change in employment status without the express notification from management of a change in that status.

Company Waiting Period – the first 90 days after hire. During this period, employees are ineligible for employment benefits unless specific benefit details require an alternate waiting period duration.

Performance Evaluation and Merit-Based Pay Increases

We feel that you have the ability to be a strong asset to our company; however, even the best employees have room for improvement. Because of this, Friendly Fence & Roofing will create an ongoing dialogue with each employee regarding his/her performance. This dialogue will include both acknowledging the employee’s strengths and a frank and honest assessment of areas for improvement. Formal performance evaluations may also be provided; however, these may or may not occur on a set timetable, and they may or may not be associated with any changes in pay status. This system is designed to provide a basis for better understanding between you, your supervisor, and Friendly Fence & Roofing regarding your job performance, potential, and development within the company.

Friendly Fence & Roofing reserves the right to establish all pay system and pay rates. Pay increases occur more regularly in some job descriptions than others. Regardless, pay increases are based on several factors, including the overall success of Friendly Fence & Roofing. Other factors that may qualify employees for an increase in pay include: job performance, productivity, your current salary in your position's grade level, and your level of pay relative to what the industry is paying for similar qualities and talent. Please note: pay increases are not made based upon a set timetable.

Separation from Employment

As a reflection of Friendly Fence & Roofing status as an at-will employer, both Friendly Fence & Roofing and its employees may choose to end the employment relationship at any time, either with notice or without notice. However, Friendly Fence & Roofing requests that employees provide at least a 2-week notice of separation stating the employee’s final date of employment and the employee’s reason for separation. This notice may impact the employee’s eligibility for rehire, as well as any information provided to any future companies seeking employment verification. Similarly, when Friendly Fence & Roofing initiates a separation that is unrelated to an employee’s conduct, Friendly Fence & Roofing will attempt to provide notice to the employee.

Upon separation, employees will be paid for any pay outlined in the employee’s pay agreement. This will include all earned forms of non-discretionary pay. However, employees are ineligible for any fringe benefits, including discretionary pay (e.g., year-end bonuses, bonuses based upon overall company success), during the last month of his/her employment.

Employees will NOT be paid for any accrued but unused paid time off (PTO) upon separation of employment.Upon termination of employment, employees are required to return all issued Planet property. Examples of Friendly Fence & Roofing property include, but are not limited to, uniforms, credit cards, cellular telephones, and keys/access cards. Failure to do so may be considered theft, and Friendly Fence & Roofing reserves the right to take any and all legally available measures necessary to obtain stolen property.

An employee’s final paycheck may be issued Via Direct Deposit regardless of the employee’s participation in any direct deposit programs.

Work Week Logistics

The official work week for Friendly Fence & Roofing is from Friday at 12:00 am until Thursday at 11:59 pm. The Friendly Fence & Roofing office is generally open Monday through Friday from 7:00 am until 6:00 pm.

An employee’s work schedule is likely to vary either seasonally or each week based upon the anticipated and actual call volume. Although we attempt to schedule an 8-hour workday, employees are not guaranteed a full 8 hours of work, especially during our slower seasons. In addition, field employees are expected to remain working until their last call of the day has been completed safely and fully. Failure to do so will be considered a violation of this policy, and it may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment. Finally, employees may be required to work overtime when call volume demands. Please see the below “Overtime” policy for more information.

Breaks for Nursing Mothers

In accordance with federal legislation, Friendly Fence & Roofing will grant sufficient breaks to nursing mothers of infants under 12 months of age in order to express breast milk during the day. Nursing mothers should speak with management for additional information.

Overtime

There may be times when we cannot meet the needs of our customers during our standard business hours. When this occurs, employees may be required to work additional hours. Overtime hours may, at times, be assigned to individuals who volunteer; however, workload may demand that all employees work more than 40 hours in any one workweek. When overtime is mandatory, hours will be distributed as equitably as possible.

If an employee has not been assigned overtime hours, he/she MUST receive managerial approval prior to working overtime hours. Failure to do so will be considered a violation of this policy.

As required by law, all employees will be compensated for overtime based upon hours worked. Any benefit hours, such as paid time off (PTO), holiday, or other leave of absence time, will not be considered when determining and compensating for overtime.

Overtime is paid to all non-exempt employees according to state and federal regulations. All overtime compensation will be paid at an employee’s “regular rate of pay,” which includes all non-discretionary forms of compensation. Overtime premium pay will be provided for all hours worked in excess of forty (40) hours in any one workweek, and compensation will be equal to one and one-half times the employee’s regular rate of pay.

On-Call Status

As a residential service provider, Friendly Fence & Roofing responds to customers' emergencies 24 hours a day. To provide this service, employees who have specific job descriptions are expected to accept on-call status when requested by management. Employees will be informed if mandatory on-call status applies to them.

The following policies apply to on-call status:

Employees are expected to wear any assigned uniform when responding to all calls for service, even while on-call.

Employees on on-call status are expected to respond, via telephone, to a customer within 30 minutes of the customer’s original call.

It is the assigned employee’s responsibility to be on-call for the entire day, not just the night, if he/she is on-call on a holiday or weekend day.

The assigned employee is responsible for finding a replacement to cover his/her on-call time if he/she is on vacation when scheduled to be on-call. Management will assist employees who have a bona fide illness while on call.

Mandatory Company Meetings and On the Job Training

Friendly Fence & Roofing conducts meetings and company-wide training programs on a regular basis. When notified by management, employees are required to attend these meetings and programs as a mandatory requirement of their positions. Failure to do so will be considered an absence, and such absence will be evaluated in accordance with Friendly Fence & Roofing’s attendance policy.

In addition to company-wide training, supervisors are responsible for identifying and ensuring implementation of any needed on-the-job training for all employees who directly report to the supervisor. This type of training is generally based upon an employee’s specific need; however, it could also include additional training on new technologies, techniques, or growth opportunities. Examples may include one-on-one training with the supervisor or other employee, safety training in addition to standard safety meetings, participation in off-site training, and continuing education.

Training and meetings, when mandatory, will be conducted during regular working hours whenever possible.

Friendly Fence & Roofing will pay for any required training programs, including tuition costs and, unless specifically addressed as part of a disciplinary action, the employee’s time while attending mandatory training.

Employees may be tested from time to time to evaluate the effectiveness of any training program.

If you have any questions regarding mandatory meetings or training, please contact your supervisor.

State of Emergency/Inclement Weather

Management may, at times, choose to temporarily cease business operations due to extreme weather or other event. Examples include, but are not limited to, a blizzard, hurricane, forest fire, or earthquake. If management decides that Friendly Fence & Roofing will close, management will inform each employee by contacting the phone number he/she has on record and/or his/her assigned company-owned cell phone. A voicemail or text will be left if an employee cannot be directly reached.

Please note: although management will attempt to notify each employee, it is not management’s responsibility to ensure that each employee has actually received notification. Employees are responsible for ensuring that his/her phone number on file is up-to-date, and employees are also responsible for listening to any voicemails or reading any texts sent.

If an employee has NOT been notified that Friendly Fence & Roofing has ceased business operations, the employee should assume that Friendly Fence & Roofing will remain open for business. The employee should report to work as normal.

Especially if an employee lives in an area that is distant from Friendly Fence & Roofing main office, management encourages that employee to use his/her best discretion regarding the conditions in his/her area of residence, as well as the areas through which the employee would need to travel. Even when management chooses to still provide standard or reduced/emergency only business operations, employees may request leave if he/she feels that the conditions in his/her area of residence or logical path of travel present a significant safety hazard. However, management reserves the right to also evaluate safety conditions, and employees may be held liable for abuse of the emergency leave policy.

In the event that the mayor, governor, president, or other government official declares a state of emergency or a mandatory evacuation impacting either the employee’s home or Friendly Fence & Roofing office, Friendly Fence & Roofing will not retaliate in any way against an employee for not reporting for work as scheduled.

Any time taken off based upon inclement weather, states of emergency, or mandatory evacuations will be on an unpaid basis, regardless of whether management closes Friendly Fence & Roofing’ office. However, employees may choose to use any accrued but unused paid time off (PTO) during this unpaid leave.

Contagious Illnesses

Friendly Fence & Roofing shares concerns with many of its employees to reduce the chance of transmission of serious illnesses within our company. Because of this, we request that employees do not report to work if they are experiencing any extreme symptoms of illness. Although we request that employees “self-regulate” these symptoms, management may require employees stay home when experiencing symptoms.

Extreme symptoms include, but are not limited to:

Fever over 100°F

Vomiting or diarrhea

Severe sore throat

Severe headache or body aches not related to overexertion or injury

Excessive coughing or sneezing

Please note: if an employee is experiencing the above extreme symptoms and those extreme symptoms are the result of a medical condition that is not contagious (e.g., pregnancy or chronic condition), the employee is not required to stay home.

Management reserves the right to require employees to provide doctor’s certification for an employee’s fitness to resume full job duties after extended or regular absences. Furthermore, abuse of this policy will be considered a violation and may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment.

Paydays and Time Records

In accordance with all applicable state and federal laws, Friendly Fence & Roofing will compensate you for all of your time worked. To help ensure that employees are paid properly and no improper deductions are made, employees are responsible for:

accurately recording all time worked, including all travel and training time;

reviewing his/her time records for any unintentional errors prior to payroll submission;

ensuring all of the employee’s time records are submitted according to procedures established for his/her department;

submitting all vacation and/or leave hours based upon procedures established for his/her department, including all required signatures and/or approvals;

reviewing his/her paycheck promptly for any errors; and

immediately reporting any errors to management.

Please note: employees are strictly prohibited from engaging in “off-the-clock” work.

Time records not submitted on time and according to established procedures may result in errors in the employee’s pay, and correction of any errors may be delayed until subsequent pay periods.

Deductions from Pay

Friendly Fence & Roofing will automatically comply with all federal and state mandated deductions. Examples include federal, state, and/or local taxes and social security.

In addition to standard mandatory deductions made for all employees, Friendly Fence & Roofing will comply with all valid claims against the wages of employees, such as wage garnishments, child support orders, and other legally valid claims. An employee will be notified about the details of the garnishment or wage order. Please note: even if an employee is attempting to address financial difficulties with a creditor, Friendly Fence & Roofing is legally required to comply with all garnishment notices or orders as soon as they are received.

In addition to mandatory deductions, some employees may also elect to have specific voluntary deductions withheld for certain things, such as health insurance premiums or contributions to a retirement plan. All voluntary deductions will be presented to each employee for written approval prior to deductions being made.

Exempt Employee Deductions

The Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) limits the types of deductions that may be made from the pay of an exempt employee. In addition to those deductions outlined above, Friendly Fence & Roofing is permitted, by this statute, to make deductions for the following reasons:

Absence from work for one or more full days for personal reasons other than sickness or disability;

Absence from work for one or more full days due to sickness or disability of the employee;

Offset for amounts received as witness or jury fees, or for military pay;

Unpaid disciplinary suspensions of one or more full days for workplace misconduct; or

During the week an exempt employee begins work for the company or last week of employment, the employee will only be paid for actual hours worked.

Please note: Exempt employees will be required to use accrued paid time off (PTO) for full or partial day absences for personal reasons, sickness, or disability. However, an exempt employee’s pay will not be reduced for partial day absences if he/she has exhausted his/her PTO.

If an employee classified as exempt believes that an improper deduction has been taken from his/her pay, the employee should immediately report the error to management. The situation will be promptly investigated, and if it is found that an improper deduction has been made, Friendly Fence & Roofing will reimburse the employee for the improper deduction.

Time Records

Employees are responsible for ensuring that their time records are completed. It is considered a violation of this policy for an employee to:

Complete another employee’s time record;

Ask, allow, or require another employee to complete your time record;

Alter a time record with false information; or

Conceal or falsify a time record.

If any manager or employee asks you to violate any of the above policies or you become aware of another employee doing so, report the violation immediately to management.

Any violations of this policy may lead to disciplinary action, up to and including immediate termination of employment.

Paydays

Employees are paid on a weekly basis, resulting in approximately fifty-two (52) paydays every calendar year. Employees are paid every Friday for work completed during the previous pay period. Friendly Fence & Roofing’ official seven-day workweek is from 12:00 a.m. Friday through 11:59 p.m. the following Thursday.

Normally, an employee’s pay is deposited directly into his/her bank account(s). Employees are eligible for direct deposit immediately upon hire, and they sign up for this program through filling out the appropriate paperwork and submitting it to management. Employees may adjust what bank account(s) are being used at any time through a resubmission of the required paperwork. Employees in the direct deposit program receive electronic access to a non-negotiable check stub detailing his/her earnings each payday. For more information, please speak with management.

At times, traditional paper paychecks may be issued to employees for a variety of reasons. These paychecks are normally available by the end of the business day on the relevant payday, and an employee may pick up his/her paycheck at the main office. Unless another pickup method is negotiated by management, only the employee is permitted to pick up his/her paycheck. Your immediate supervisor will inform you if paper paychecks will be issued and will clarify any relevant pickup procedures.

If a payday falls on a holiday, paychecks will be available the business day before the holiday unless Friendly Fence & Roofing specifies otherwise. Under no other circumstances will checks be distributed early.

Employees should verify all paychecks immediately upon receipt. Any employee who feels that his/her paycheck reflects an error should report his/her concerns to his/her supervisor and/or management. Unfortunately, mistakes can occur, and any allegations of a mistake brought to our attention will be promptly investigated and corrected.

Employees who report a mistake in pay or other violations of this policy or who assist in any investigation of violations will not be subject to any form of retaliation.

Company Gas Cards

Based upon business considerations, some employees are issued company gas cards to use for business-related purchases. Company cards may only be used for authorized purchases.

Company gas cards are issued for a specific vehicle. They may only be used to purchase gasoline for the specific vehicle for which they are issued, and the card should be kept in a secure, out-of-sight location in its assigned vehicle.

Employees may NOT use any company card for personal purchases.

Employees are responsible for any cards assigned to them. Lost or stolen cards must be reported to management immediately. Furthermore, use of company cards by individuals other than the assigned employee is forbidden.

Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

Expense Reimbursement

Some employees, through the nature of their work for Friendly Fence & Roofing, may be required to initially pay for certain business-related purchases. Although this is likely to be rare, if it does occur, employees must obtain and submit an itemized receipt to management for reimbursement. Purchases must be pre-approved by management, and all receipts must be turned in no more than one month after the purchase.

If incurred expenses are related to employee travel, additional procedures may apply. Management will communicate additional expectations and procedures to impacted employees prior to any relevant company-related travel.

Failure to follow any policies or procedures related to expense reimbursement may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment.

Access to Personnel Files

Employee files are maintained by management and are considered confidential. Employees of Friendly Fence & Roofing only have access to personnel file information on a need-to-know basis.

Current and former employees wishing to access their own personnel files may do so by contacting Human Resources. Human Resources will generally arrange for a review upon request within 3 days of the request. Personnel files are to be reviewed in the main office at a location provided by management. Employee files may not be taken away from the designated location. Representatives of government or law enforcement agencies, in the course of their duties, may be allowed access to file information.

Employee Image Use

Friendly Fence & Roofing may take photographs and videos during working hours or during work-related functions of any or all employees. Pictures and videos taken of employees while participating in Friendly Fence & Roofing functions remain the property of Friendly Fence & Roofing. As such, these pictures and videos may be used for business-related purposes, including, but not limited to, the company website, social media, marketing, and training materials. Friendly Fence & Roofing is under no obligation to remove any pictures or videos taken of an employee after separation from employment, regardless of whether that separation is initiated by the employee or Friendly Fence & Roofing.

The creation and use of pictures and videos of an employee does not create an employment contract and in no way alter the employment at-will policy of Friendly Fence & Roofing.

Drug-Free and Alcohol-Free Workplace

Although Friendly Fence & Roofing respects an employee’s personal choices with respect to drug and alcohol use, Friendly Fence & Roofing is concerned about the use of these substances, whether on or off the job, if it adversely affects an employee's work performance, efficiency, safety, or health. As a reflection of this concern, Friendly Fence & Roofing has established the following Drug-Free and Alcohol-Free Workplace policy. The following are strictly prohibited by Friendly Fence & Roofing:

Possessing, using, or being under the influence of alcohol, an illegal substance, or a controlled substance during working hours or while driving a company-owned vehicle.

2. Distributing, selling, or purchasing alcohol, an illegal substance, or a controlled substance during working hours or while driving a company-owned vehicle.

Use of prescription and/or over-the-counter drugs may also affect an employee's job performance and ability to perform his/her job safely. If an employee is using a prescription medication or over-the-counter medication in a lawful manner, and that medication does not impact the employee’s ability to safely and effectively perform his/her duties, the previous restrictions do not apply. However, if an employee is using prescription and/or over-the-counter drugs that may impair the employee's ability to safely perform the job or affect the safety or well-being of others, he/she should notify his/her supervisor immediately. An employee may be required to provide a doctor’s verification regarding the employee’s need to take the medication. The employee may be granted a leave of absence for the duration for which he/she will be taking the medication. If available, the employee will be required to use any accrued paid time off (PTO) during this time period. If no paid leave is available, the leave of absence may be granted on an unpaid basis.

Please note: the use of marijuana or its chemical derivatives during work hours has been deemed to be a safety hazard to employees, our customers, and the general public. Its use also negatively impacts our employee’s ability to provide acceptable levels of customer service.
